Headline: Trivandrum in a Day
Description: One guide, read once, and you're ready. Trivandrum's temples, museums and beaches in one shared-seat day: the route, what to expect at each stop, what to carry, and how to book.
Highlights: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, Museum Junction, Lunch, Veli Tourist Village
Itinerary:
7:45 AM Pickup — Trivandrum Central / East Fort / Trivandrum Airport: Choose any of the three pickup points. Guests board; water and snack packs handed out for the day.
8:15 AM — Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple: Exterior and heritage-architecture view for non-Hindu guests. Interior access is Hindus-only with a strict dress code, flagged clearly before booking.
9:15 AM — Museum Junction: Napier Museum, the Zoo, Kanakakunnu Palace grounds and Sree Chitra Art Gallery, all within walking distance.
12:30 PM — Lunch: Own expense, or a paid add-on at a partner restaurant — guest's choice at booking.
1:30 PM — Veli Tourist Village: Lagoon, floating bridge and optional boating.
3:00 PM — Chalai Bazaar: Flex stop for local market browsing; skipped if the day is running long.
4:00 PM — Shankumugham Beach: Free entry, close to base: the day's sunset-and-photos finish.
5:15 PM Drop-off — Central, East Fort, the Airport — or your own stop: A different drop within the city is free; a small surcharge applies beyond a set radius.
Good_To_Know:
🛕 Padmanabhaswamy Temple: Interior access is for Hindus only, with a strict dress code. Non-Hindu guests get an exterior and heritage-architecture view. Ask us about the dress code when you book.
🏛️ Museum Junction: Napier Museum, the Zoo, Kanakakunnu and Sree Chitra Art Gallery are within walking distance. Entry is included in your seat. Napier and Sree Chitra are closed on Mondays.
🚣 Veli & 🛍️ Chalai: Boating at Veli is optional. Chalai Bazaar is a flex stop: we may skip it if the day runs long.
🏖️ Shankumugham Beach: Free entry, close to base. The relaxed, photos-and-sea-breeze finish to the day.
Exclusions: Lunch (own expense or partner restaurant add-on); Veli boating (optional)
What_To_Carry: Comfortable walking shoes; Clothing suitable for temple visits; Cash for lunch and optional boating; Your phone, charged, with our number saved

Headline: Coastal Trail
Description: One guide for the coast south of the city: Kovalam's lighthouse beaches, the Vizhinjam seaport and the Poovar backwaters. The route, the extras to budget for, what to carry, and how to book.
Highlights: Kovalam — Lighthouse, Hawa & Samudra Beaches, Vizhinjam Seaport Viewpoint & Fishing Harbour, Lunch, Poovar Backwaters
Itinerary:
9:00 AM Pickup — Trivandrum Central / East Fort / Trivandrum Airport: Choose any of the three pickup points. Guests board; water and snack packs handed out. About 16 km down the coast road to the first stop.
9:30 AM — Kovalam — Lighthouse, Hawa & Samudra Beaches: Three linked crescent beaches below a rocky headland. Climb the working lighthouse for a coastal panorama, swim, or walk the promenade.
11:30 AM — Vizhinjam Seaport Viewpoint & Fishing Harbour: A short stop at India's newest deepwater transshipment port, 3 km south of Kovalam: ship-spotting alongside one of Kerala's busiest fishing harbours.
12:15 PM — Lunch: Own expense, or a paid add-on at a seafood restaurant near the harbour — guest's choice at booking.
2:00 PM — Poovar Backwaters: About 17 km on from Vizhinjam. A mangrove-lined channel leads to the golden sand bar where the Neyyar river meets the Arabian Sea. Boating is optional, paid directly to the boat operator at the jetty.
3:15 PM — Poovar Sand Bar — free time: Swim in the calm backwater on one side or the open sea on the other, with the day's best light for photos.
6:00 PM Drop-off — Central, East Fort, the Airport — or your own stop: A different drop within the city is free; a small surcharge applies beyond a set radius.
Good_To_Know:
🗼 Kovalam: Three crescent beaches: Lighthouse, Hawa and Samudra. Lighthouse climb is about ₹30, own expense. Swim or walk the promenade.
🚢 Vizhinjam: A short stop at India's newest deepwater transshipment port. Ship-spotting next to a busy fishing harbour.
🛶 Poovar boating: Not bundled: pay the boat operator directly. Some private clubs quote far above the notified fare. Ask for the government-notified rate. Our team will guide you at the jetty.
🏝️ Poovar Sand Bar: Calm backwater on one side, open sea on the other. Free time to swim and take photos.
Exclusions: Lunch (own expense or seafood add-on); Lighthouse climb (~₹30); Poovar boating (optional)
What_To_Carry: Swimwear and a towel; Sunscreen, hat and sunglasses; Cash for the boat and lighthouse; A change of clothes

Headline: Varkala Cliff Day
Description: One guide for a full day at Kerala's only cliff-backed beach: the holy Papanasam spring, Sivagiri Mutt and the cliff-top promenade. The route, the optional paragliding, what to carry, and how to book.
Highlights: Varkala Cliff & Papanasam Beach, Papanasam Spring & Janardanaswamy Temple, Free time & lunch, Sivagiri Mutt
Itinerary:
8:00 AM Pickup — Trivandrum Central / East Fort / Trivandrum Airport: Choose any of the three pickup points. Guests board; water and snack packs handed out. About 42 km north, roughly 1.5 hours.
9:30 AM — Varkala Cliff & Papanasam Beach: Kerala's only beach backed by sheer red laterite cliffs: a cliff-top promenade of cafés and shops above, open beach below.
10:15 AM — Papanasam Spring & Janardanaswamy Temple: A natural spring at the base of the cliff, believed to wash away sins ("Papanasam" means exactly that), beside a Vishnu temple over a thousand years old.
11:30 AM — Free time & lunch: Cliff-top cafés, own expense. Varkala's promenade has the widest food choice of any kfGo tour.
1:00 PM — Sivagiri Mutt: Hilltop ashram of Sree Narayana Guru, one of Kerala's most significant social reformers: a quiet, garden-set pilgrimage site a short drive from the cliff.
2:30 PM — Back to the cliff — paragliding (optional): Seasonal and weather-permitting: a 15–20 minute tandem flight off the cliff with a licensed operator, paid direct.
4:30 PM — Sunset at the cliff: Varkala's signature moment: the sun dropping into the Arabian Sea, seen from the cliff edge.
6:30 PM Drop-off — Central, East Fort, the Airport — or your own stop: A different drop within the city is free; a small surcharge applies beyond a set radius.
Good_To_Know:
🏖️ Varkala Cliff: Sheer red laterite cliffs above Papanasam Beach. Cliff-top cafés and shops; the widest food choice of any kfGo tour.
🛕 Papanasam Spring & Temple: A natural spring believed to wash away sins. Beside the Janardanaswamy Vishnu temple, over a thousand years old.
🕊️ Sivagiri Mutt: Hilltop ashram of Sree Narayana Guru. A quiet pilgrimage site: please dress and behave respectfully.
🪂 Paragliding: 15–20 minute tandem flight off the cliff. Depends on season and wind on the day. Not bundled into the kfGo price.
Exclusions: Lunch at cliff-top cafés; Paragliding (optional)
What_To_Carry: Swimwear and a towel; Sunscreen and a hat; Modest clothing for the temple and Sivagiri; Cash or card for cafés and paragliding

Headline: Kollam Backwaters
Description: One guide for our farthest tour north: Thangassery lighthouse and fort, the eight-armed Ashtamudi Lake and Kollam's quieter beaches. The route, the optional lake cruise, what to carry, and how to book.
Highlights: Thangassery Lighthouse & Fort, Thangassery Beach, Ashtamudi Lake, Lunch
Itinerary:
7:30 AM Pickup — Trivandrum Central / East Fort / Trivandrum Airport: Choose any of the three pickup points. Guests board; water and snack packs handed out. About 66 km north, roughly 2 hours.
9:30 AM — Thangassery Lighthouse & Fort: One of Kerala's oldest working lighthouses (1902), on the site of an old Portuguese fort. Climb for a coastal view, with the fort ruins and St. Thomas Church alongside.
10:30 AM — Thangassery Beach: A quieter beach right beside the lighthouse — a walk, not a crowd.
11:15 AM — Ashtamudi Lake: Kerala's second-largest wetland and the backwaters' southern gateway; eight interlocking channels give it its name ("ashta" = eight, "mudi" = branch). Shikara or houseboat cruises available at the jetty.
1:00 PM — Lunch: Own expense, or a paid add-on. Kollam is Kerala's historic cashew-processing hub, so ask for it on the menu.
2:00 PM — Thirumullavaram Beach: A calmer alternative to the lighthouse beach, with a small shoreline temple: good for a slower afternoon stop.
3:15 PM — Kollam Town — Chinnakada: Flex stop at the town centre's landmark clock tower and market area; skipped if the day is running long.
6:30 PM Drop-off — Central, East Fort, the Airport — or your own stop: A different drop within the city is free; a small surcharge applies beyond a set radius.
Good_To_Know:
🗼 Thangassery: One of Kerala's oldest working lighthouses (1902), on an old Portuguese fort site. Lighthouse entry is your own expense. Fort ruins and St. Thomas Church alongside.
🛶 Ashtamudi Lake: Kerala's second-largest wetland; 'ashta' = eight, 'mudi' = branch. Shikara or houseboat cruise optional, paid direct.
🌊 The beaches: Thangassery Beach: a walk, not a crowd. Thirumullavaram: calmer, with a small shoreline temple.
🕰️ Kollam town: Chinnakada clock tower and market: a flex stop. Kollam is Kerala's cashew hub, so ask for it at lunch.
Exclusions: Lunch (own expense or add-on); Lighthouse entry; Lake cruise (optional)
What_To_Carry: Sunscreen and a hat; Comfortable shoes for the lighthouse climb; Cash for entry and the cruise; A light snack for the 2-hour drive

Headline: Jatayu & Varkala
Description: One guide for our longest day: the world's largest bird sculpture at Jatayu Earth's Center, Kerala's only cable car, and an unhurried finish on the Varkala cliffs. The route, the optional adventures, what to carry, and how to book.
Highlights: Jatayu Earth's Center — the sculpture & cable car, Museum, 360° deck & the Jatayu–Ravana theatre, Hill 2 forest trek (optional), Adventure Park (optional)
Itinerary:
7:00 AM Pickup — Trivandrum Central / East Fort / Trivandrum Airport: Choose any of the three pickup points. Guests board; water and snack packs handed out. About 50 km inland, roughly 1.3 hours on MC Road (SH-1).
8:20 AM — Jatayu Earth's Center — the sculpture & cable car: A 200-foot bird sculpture atop Jatayu Rock Hill, billed as the world's largest, built around the Ramayana legend of the eagle who fought Ravana to defend Sita. Kerala's only cable car carries you up.
9:30 AM — Museum, 360° deck & the Jatayu–Ravana theatre: Exhibition rooms inside the sculpture, an observation deck in its head, and a multi-dimensional mini theatre staging the legendary battle.
10:45 AM — Hill 2 forest trek (optional): A guided hour through the park's private forest on the second hill: quieter and greener than the sculpture crowds.
11:45 AM — Adventure Park (optional): Up to twenty activities, from zip-lining and archery to paintball and rappelling, priced by the park itself.
12:30 PM — Drive on to Varkala: Only 27 km further, about 40 minutes: the short hop that makes pairing the two worthwhile.
1:15 PM — Lunch, Varkala cliff-top: Own expense, at one of the cliff-top restaurants overlooking Papanasam Beach.
2:15 PM — Varkala Cliff & Papanasam Beach — free time: Kerala's only beach backed by sheer red laterite cliffs, with the cliff-top promenade for an unhurried finish to the day.
6:15 PM Drop-off — Central, East Fort, the Airport — or your own stop: About 42 km back, roughly 1.3 hours. Free drop within the city; a small surcharge beyond a set radius.
Good_To_Know:
🦅 Jatayu Earth's Center: A 200-foot sculpture on Jatayu Rock Hill, from the Ramayana legend. Kerala's only cable car carries you up: included.
🏛️ Inside the sculpture: Museum rooms, a 360° deck in the head, and a mini theatre of the Jatayu–Ravana battle.
🧗 Optional extras: Hill 2 guided forest trek (optional). Adventure Park activities, paid direct to the park.
🏖️ Varkala Cliff: Lunch at a cliff-top restaurant, own expense. Free time on the promenade. Paragliding optional, seasonal, paid direct.
Exclusions: Adventure Park (optional); Lunch at Varkala; Paragliding (optional)
What_To_Carry: Comfortable shoes for the rock hill; Sunscreen, hat and water; Cash or card for adventure activities; Your phone, charged, for the 360° views

Headline: Kanyakumari Day Trip
Description: One guide for India's southernmost tip, where three seas meet: Padmanabhapuram Palace, Suchindram temple, the Vivekananda Rock Memorial and the Thiruvalluvar Statue. The route, closures to plan around, what to carry, and how to book.
Highlights: Padmanabhapuram Palace, Suchindram Thanumalayan Temple, Arulmigu Bhagavathy Amman Temple, Kanyakumari Beach — the three seas confluence
Itinerary:
7:30 AM Pickup — Trivandrum Central / East Fort / Trivandrum Airport: Water and snacks handed out. About 90 km south-east, roughly 3 hours.
9:00 AM — Padmanabhapuram Palace: On the way, near Thuckalay: the old Travancore palace, famous for its carved wooden halls and murals.
10:15 AM — Suchindram Thanumalayan Temple: A rare trimurti temple with musical stone pillars. Free entry.
11:15 AM — Arulmigu Bhagavathy Amman Temple: The temple the town is named for, near the beach.
12:00 PM — Kanyakumari Beach — the three seas confluence: Where the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal and Indian Ocean meet.
12:45 PM — Lunch: Own expense, at one of the seafront restaurants in Kanyakumari town.
2:00 PM — Vivekananda Rock Memorial & Thiruvalluvar Statue: A short ferry to the twin rock islets: the memorial where Swami Vivekananda is said to have meditated, and the 133-foot Thiruvalluvar Statue beside it.
4:00 PM — Kanyakumari Lighthouse & Sunset Point: A working lighthouse beside the point where locals gather in the evening. The drive home means an early-evening view rather than the full sunset.
8:00 PM Drop-off — Central, East Fort, the Airport — or your own stop: About 90 km back, roughly 3 hours. Free drop within the city; a small surcharge beyond a set radius.
Good_To_Know:
🛕 Suchindram Temple: A rare trimurti temple: Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma in one sanctum. Famous for its musical stone pillars. Free entry; donation-based.
🏯 Padmanabhapuram Palace: The old Travancore royal palace, known for its carved wooden halls. Closed on Mondays; entry is your own expense. Shoes are removed inside.
⛴️ Rock Memorial: Short ferry to the twin rock islets. Vivekananda memorial and the 133-foot Thiruvalluvar Statue. Closed on Tuesdays.
🙏 Amman Temple: The temple the town is named for. Open mornings until 12:30 PM — we visit at 11:15 AM. Dress code applies.
Exclusions: Lunch at seafront restaurants; Palace entry; Temple donations (optional)
What_To_Carry: Modest clothing for temple visits; Original photo ID; Sunscreen and a hat; A light jacket for the evening drive back

Headline: Sabarimala pilgrimage
Description: Whole-vehicle pilgrimage from Trivandrum to the Nilakkal base camp: pickup, the drive, no waiting charges while you complete darshan, and the drive home. Full Traveller works out to ₹917 per pilgrim.
Highlights: Nilakkal base camp, No waiting charges, Pickup home/station/airport, Hatchback to Traveller
Inclusions: Vehicle and driver for the day; No waiting charges at Nilakkal; Driver bata
Exclusions: KSRTC Nilakkal–Pampa bus; Food, stay, offerings
What_To_Carry: Virtual Queue coupon (printed); Original photo ID; Irumudi; Change of clothes

Headline: Kochi Airport door to door
Description: Flying out of Cochin International? Start from your own doorstep in Trivandrum and step out at the terminal — or land in Kochi and we bring you home.
Highlights: Doorstep pickup, ~245 km, 5–6 hrs, Departures drop-off, Arrivals pickup too
Itinerary:
Pickup — Your door: Home, hotel, Central, East Fort or Trivandrum Airport — at the time we agree for your flight.
On the road — ~245 km on NH 66: About 5–6 hours via Kollam and Alappuzha, with a refreshment stop on the way.
Drop-off — Cochin International Airport: Departures at Nedumbassery. Reverse trips start from the arrivals hall. (No waiting charges on arrivals)
Good_To_Know:
✈️ Timing your trip: Plan to reach the airport 3 hours before an international flight and 2 hours before a domestic one. Share your flight number so we can track delays.
🧳 Luggage: Hatchbacks and sedans suit 2–3 people with check-in bags. Families with large bags: choose an MPV, Premium SUV or Traveller.
🔁 Return trips: Arriving in Kochi? We pick you up from arrivals. Up to 1 hour of waiting is included for flight delays.
📍 Other Kochi drops: Kochi city, Fort Kochi or a hotel in Ernakulam? Ask us for a quote.
Inclusions: Door-to-door pickup; No waiting charges on arrivals; Driver bata; Fuel and per-km charges
Exclusions: Tolls and airport parking
What_To_Carry: Passport / ID and tickets; Flight number shared with us; A light snack for the drive

Headline: Alappuzha backwaters
Description: A private day on Kerala's famous backwaters: a cruise through Vembanad's canals, a Kerala meal and an evening on Alappuzha beach.
Highlights: Backwater cruise, Kerala lunch, Alappuzha Beach, Krishnapuram Palace
Itinerary:
6:30 AM — Pickup: Home, hotel, Central, East Fort or Trivandrum Airport
10:00 AM — Backwater cruise: Shikara or day houseboat through the canals and paddy fields of the Vembanad backwaters. (Cruise paid direct to the operator)
1:00 PM — Kerala lunch: Own expense — try karimeen (pearl spot) on a banana leaf.
2:30 PM — Alappuzha Beach & lighthouse: The old pier, the lighthouse and the long sandy beach.
4:00 PM — Krishnapuram Palace (on the way back): 18th-century Travancore palace at Kayamkulam, home to a famous Gajendra Moksham mural. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
8:30 PM — Drop-off: Back to your door or any point in Trivandrum.
Good_To_Know:
🛶 Choosing a boat: Shikara: small, canopy boat, best for 2–6 people for a few hours. Day houseboat: lunch on board, best for families. Overnight houseboat? Ask us to plan a 2-day trip.
💰 Paying for the boat: The cruise isn't in our price — pay the operator directly. Agree the hours and route before you board.
🏛️ Krishnapuram Palace: Closed on Mondays. On a Monday we add more beach time instead.
🌧️ Weather: Best from September to March. In heavy rain, cruises may be shortened.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver; No waiting charges; Driver bata; Free drop anywhere in the city
Exclusions: Boat cruise; Lunch; Palace entry; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Sunscreen and hat; Cash for the boat; Light cotton clothes

Headline: Vagamon meadows & pines
Description: Rolling green meadows, pine forests and misty viewpoints — Kerala's quietest hill escape, about five hours from Trivandrum.
Highlights: Pine forest, Meadows & lake, Kurisumala, Paragliding (opt.)
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:30 AM — Pickup & drive: About 190 km via Kottayam and Erattupetta, roughly 5 hours.
Day 1 · afternoon — Pine forest & Vagamon meadows: Walk the pine valley and the rolling grass hills.
Day 1 · evening — Vagamon Lake: A calm lake ringed by tea and meadows. Overnight in Vagamon. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Kurisumala & Murugan Mala: Hilltop pilgrimage sites with sweeping valley views.
Day 2 · late morning — Paragliding (optional): Seasonal tandem flights at the Vagamon launch site. (Paid direct · weather-dependent)
Day 2 · ~8 PM — Home: Drive back to your door in Trivandrum.
Good_To_Know:
🌲 Pine forest & meadows: Wear grippy shoes — slopes are slippery after rain. Mornings are misty; afternoons clearer.
🪂 Paragliding: Runs in season, weather-permitting. Not in our price — pay the operator directly.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel or homestay; we can suggest areas. Your driver stays nearby — his night allowance is in our price.
🧥 Weather: Cool evenings — bring a light jacket. Best from September to May.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; Sightseeing in Vagamon; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Paragliding and entry fees; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Light jacket; Walking shoes; Raincoat or umbrella; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Munnar tea hills
Description: Endless tea gardens, waterfalls on the way up, and the Nilgiri tahr of Eravikulam — Kerala's favourite hill station at your own pace.
Highlights: Tea gardens, Eravikulam Park, Waterfalls, Top Station
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive up: About 290 km via Kothamangalam, roughly 7–8 hours.
Day 1 · afternoon — Cheeyappara & Valara waterfalls: Roadside waterfalls on the climb into the hills. Overnight in Munnar. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Eravikulam National Park: Rajamala, home of the Nilgiri tahr. Park buses take you up. (Entry paid direct · usually closed for calving ~Feb–Mar)
Day 2 · midday — Tea Museum: How tea goes from leaf to cup in Munnar. (Entry own expense)
Day 2 · afternoon — Mattupetty Dam, Echo Point & Top Station: Lake views, boating (optional) and the valley lookout at Top Station.
Day 3 — Drive home: Leave after breakfast; back in Trivandrum by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🐐 Eravikulam: Book tickets in advance on busy days. Usually closed for the tahr calving season around February–March — check before you go.
🍃 Tea estates: Most tea gardens are private land — photograph from the roadside. Buy fresh tea at the museum or estate shops.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel; Munnar town, Chithirapuram and Pallivasal are popular. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🧥 Weather: Cold mornings, especially Dec–Jan. Hill roads are winding — carry motion sickness tablets if needed.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 3 days; All Munnar sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Park, museum and boating fees; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Warm jacket; Walking shoes; Motion sickness tablets; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Wayanad caves & forests
Description: Ancient cave carvings, misty lakes, dams and forest roads in Kerala's green north — a full road trip with your own vehicle and driver.
Highlights: Edakkal Caves, Banasura Dam, Pookode Lake, Waterfalls
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 5:30 AM — Pickup & long drive north: About 470 km via NH 66 and the Thamarassery ghat, roughly 10 hours. Overnight in Wayanad. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Edakkal Caves: A short, steep trek to caves with prehistoric rock carvings. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
Day 2 · afternoon — Banasura Sagar Dam & Phantom Rock: India's largest earth dam, with islands in the reservoir.
Day 3 · morning — Pookode Lake & Lakkidi viewpoint: A freshwater lake in the forest, and the view down the ghat. (Boating optional, paid direct)
Day 3 · afternoon — Soochipara Waterfalls: A forest walk to a tiered waterfall. (Entry own expense · check if open)
Day 4 — Drive home: Leave early; back in Trivandrum by night.
Good_To_Know:
🪨 Edakkal Caves: Closed on Mondays — we plan around it. The climb is steep: not ideal for elders or small children.
🌧️ Forest sites: Waterfalls and treks can close after heavy rain. We check on the day and swap stops if needed.
🏨 Your stay: You book your resort or homestay; Kalpetta and Vythiri are central. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🛣️ The long drive: Day 1 and Day 4 are long road days with breaks. Want it easier? Add a night in Kozhikode — ask us.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 4 days; All Wayanad sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowances; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry and boating fees; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Trekking shoes; Raincoat; Light jacket; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Ooty queen of hills
Description: The Nilgiris' classic hill stations: gardens and lakes in Ooty, tea country in Coonoor, and the famous toy train — your vehicle, your pace.
Highlights: Botanical Garden, Ooty Lake, Coonoor tea, Toy train (opt.)
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 5:30 AM — Pickup & drive: About 556 km via Palakkad, Coimbatore and Mettupalayam, roughly 11 hours. Overnight in Ooty. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Botanical Garden & Rose Garden: Ooty's best-known gardens. (Entry own expense)
Day 2 · afternoon — Ooty Lake & Doddabetta Peak: Boating (optional) and the highest point in the Nilgiris.
Day 3 · morning — Coonoor — Sim's Park & Dolphin's Nose: Tea country, gardens and a famous valley lookout.
Day 3 · optional — Nilgiri Mountain Railway: The UNESCO-listed toy train between Ooty and Coonoor. (Book tickets in advance · paid direct)
Day 4 — Drive home: Leave early; back in Trivandrum by night.
Good_To_Know:
🚂 Toy train: Seats sell out — book on IRCTC well before your trip. We meet you at the other station with your vehicle.
🪪 Tamil Nadu entry: Ooty is in Tamil Nadu: interstate permit, border tax and any hill-station e-pass are billed at actual cost. We check entry rules before you travel.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel; Ooty town and Coonoor both work well. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🧥 Weather: Cold nights all year — bring warm clothes. Ghat roads have 36 hairpin bends from Mettupalayam side.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 4 days; Ooty and Coonoor sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowances; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry, boating and toy train tickets; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Warm jacket; Photo ID; Motion sickness tablets; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Kodaikanal princess of hills
Description: A star-shaped lake, cliff-edge walks and pillar rocks in the Palani hills — Tamil Nadu's cool retreat, with your own vehicle and driver.
Highlights: Kodai Lake, Coaker's Walk, Pillar Rocks, Pine forest
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 5:30 AM — Pickup & drive: About 410 km, roughly 9–10 hours, climbing the ghat past Silver Cascade falls. Overnight in Kodaikanal. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Kodai Lake & Bryant Park: Boating or cycling round the lake, then the gardens. (Boating paid direct)
Day 2 · midday — Coaker's Walk: A cliff-edge path with views to the plains. (Entry own expense)
Day 2 · afternoon — Pillar Rocks, pine forest & Guna Caves viewpoint: Granite pillars, tall pines and the famous caves lookout.
Day 3 — Drive home: Leave after breakfast; back in Trivandrum by night.
Good_To_Know:
🪪 Tamil Nadu entry: Kodaikanal is in Tamil Nadu: interstate permit, border tax and any hill-station e-pass are billed at actual cost. We check entry rules before you travel.
🌫️ Viewpoints: Mist can hide Pillar Rocks and Coaker's Walk — mornings are usually clearer. We reorder stops for the best views.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel; near the lake is most convenient. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🧥 Weather: Cool all year, cold at night. Best from October to June.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 3 days; Kodaikanal sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowances; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry and boating fees; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Warm jacket; Photo ID; Walking shoes; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Mysore city of palaces
Description: Through Wayanad's forests and the Bandipur road to Mysore's palace, gardens and Srirangapatna — a royal road trip with your own vehicle.
Highlights: Mysore Palace, Brindavan Gardens, Bandipur forest, Chamundi Hill
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 5:30 AM — Pickup & drive to Wayanad: About 470 km, roughly 10 hours. Overnight in Wayanad. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Wayanad to Mysore via Bandipur: About 130 km through forest — watch for deer and elephants. (Bandipur road closed to traffic at night)
Day 2 · afternoon — Chamundi Hill & Brindavan Gardens: The hilltop temple, then the musical fountain at Brindavan. (Entry own expense)
Day 3 — Mysore Palace, Srirangapatna & St Philomena's: The palace, Tipu Sultan's island fort and the Gothic cathedral. (Palace lit up on Sundays and holidays, evening)
Day 4 — Drive back to Wayanad / Kozhikode: Break the return journey. Overnight on the way. (Stay booked by you)
Day 5 — Home: Back in Trivandrum by evening.
Good_To_Know:

🛕 Temple etiquette: Shoulders and knees covered; footwear off inside the shrines. The Sringeri Math closes from about 12:30 to 4 PM — that's why Kalady comes first.
⛰️ The Malayattoor climb: A steep, rocky path — allow about two hours up and down. Not for guests with knee, heart or breathing problems; they can rest at the church at the foot of the hill.
🗓️ Pilgrim season: In Lent, especially Holy Week and the Sunday after Easter, the hill takes huge crowds. On those dates we may reorder the day or skip the climb.
🐘 Abhayaranyam: Visiting hours are set by the forest department and can change. We re-confirm the day before; if it's closed, we spend the time by the Periyar.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Tower and shelter entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Comfortable walking shoes; Clothes covering shoulders and knees; Water bottle for the climb; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Palaces & temple trail
Description: The royal side of Kochi: the Chottanikkara Devi temple, the Kochi kings' Hill Palace and their temple at Tripunithura, then an afternoon of nets, crab farms and a country boat at Kumbalangi.
Highlights: Hill Palace Museum, Chottanikkara temple, Kumbalangi village, Country-boat ride
Itinerary:
8:30 AM — Pickup: Ernakulam South station · Vyttila Hub · Cochin Airport (on request) (Airport pickup on request)
9:15 AM — Chottanikkara Bhagavathy temple: One of Kerala's most visited Devi temples, with the lower Keezhkkavu shrine. (Temple dress code)
10:30 AM — Poornathrayeesa temple: The old royal temple of the Kochi kings in the heart of Tripunithura — a short stop if open. (Optional · dress code)
11:15 AM — Hill Palace Museum: The Kochi royal family's palace complex: crowns, palanquins, paintings and a deer park. Lunch in Tripunithura after, own expense. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
2:45 PM — Kumbalangi village: Kerala's model tourism village: Chinese nets, crab and fish farms, coir work and a country-boat ride on the backwaters. (Boat ride paid direct)
6:00 PM — Drop-off: Ernakulam South, Vyttila, Airport, or your own stop in the city
Good_To_Know:
🗓️ Days & timings: Hill Palace is closed on Mondays, so this tour does not run then. Temples close around midday — that's why we see them in the morning.
👗 Temple dress: Men: mundu or trousers, shirts off where asked. Women: saree, churidar or long skirt. No shorts. Some shrines admit Hindus only — non-Hindu guests can see the grounds and outside.
🛶 Kumbalangi: The country boat, fishing demos and farm visits are paid direct to the village operators. Life jackets on in the boat; no boating in storms.
🌞 Comfort: Kumbalangi is open and sunny in the afternoon — hat, sunscreen and water. Mosquitoes by the water near dusk — repellent helps.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Palace entry, boat ride & village activities; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Temple-friendly clothes; Hat and sunscreen; Mosquito repellent; Cash for entry & boat

Headline: Guruvayur day pilgrimage
Description: An early drive for darshan at Guruvayur's Sri Krishna temple and Mammiyoor, the Punnathur Kotta elephants, and an optional stop at Thrissur's Vadakkunnathan.
Highlights: Guruvayur temple, Punnathur Kotta, Mammiyoor temple, Vadakkunnathan
Itinerary:
5:00 AM — Pickup: Ernakulam South station · Vyttila Hub · Cochin Airport (on request) (Very early start)
7:00 AM — Vadakkunnathan temple, Thrissur: Quick darshan at the great Shiva temple, then breakfast in Thrissur, own expense. (Optional · Hindus only)
8:30 AM — Guruvayur Sri Krishna temple: Darshan at 'the Dwarka of the South'. Phones, bags and footwear go to the counters. (Hindus only · strict dress code)
11:45 AM — Mammiyoor Mahadeva temple: The Shiva temple next to Guruvayur. Lunch after, own expense. (Dress code)
1:30 PM — Punnathur Kotta: The temple's elephant yard in an old palace compound. (Entry own expense)
5:30 PM — Drop-off: Ernakulam South, Vyttila, Airport, or your own stop in the city
Good_To_Know:
👗 Dress code: Men: mundu, no shirt (a shawl is fine). Women: saree, churidar or long skirt. No jeans, shorts or T-shirts. Mundus and sarees are sold near the temple if needed.
📵 At the temple: Phones, cameras, bags and footwear are not allowed inside — use the paid counters. Queues of 2–4 hours on weekends, Ekadasi and wedding days; keep water and medicines handy.
🙏 Non-Hindu guests: The temples admit Hindus only. You can see the East Nada and gopuram from outside, walk the temple town and visit the elephant yard. Tell us when booking; we'll agree a comfortable meeting point.
🌙 Early start: Pickup at 5:00 AM — rest in the vehicle, breakfast in Thrissur. If queues are very long we may skip Thrissur to stay on time.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Breakfast and lunch; Offerings, special darshan & elephant-yard entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Mundu / saree / churidar; Small pouch for medicines; Water bottle; Cash for counters

Headline: Cochin airport transfer
Description: Catching a flight from Cochin International? We pick you up at your door anywhere in Kochi and drop you at the right terminal — or meet you at arrivals and bring you home.
Highlights: Doorstep pickup, ~40 km, 1–1.5 hrs, T1 / T3 drop-off, Arrivals pickup too
Itinerary:
Pickup — Your door: Home or hotel in Ernakulam, Fort Kochi, Kakkanad or anywhere in the city — at the time we agree for your flight.
On the road — ~30–45 km to Nedumbassery: About 1–1.5 hours via Edappally, Kalamassery and Aluva on NH 544 — longer at peak hours.
Drop-off — Cochin International Airport: Domestic (T1) or international (T3) departures. Reverse trips start from the arrivals exit. (No waiting charges on arrivals)
Good_To_Know:
✈️ Timing your trip: Reach the airport 3 hours before an international flight and 2 hours before a domestic one. From Fort Kochi or at peak hours (8–10 AM, 5–8 PM), allow extra time.
🛫 Which terminal?: Domestic flights use T1; international flights use T3. Check your ticket and tell us — we drop you at the right kerb.
🧳 Luggage: Hatchbacks and sedans suit 2–3 people with check-in bags. Families with large bags: choose an MPV, Premium SUV or Traveller.
🔁 Arriving in Kochi?: Share your flight number; we track delays and meet you at the arrivals exit with a name board. We track your flight — no waiting charges if it lands late.

Exclusions: Tolls and airport parking

Highlights: Doorstep pickup, ~215 km, 5–6 hrs, T1 / T2 drop-off, Arrivals pickup too

Headline: Munnar tea hills
Description: Waterfalls on the climb, tea estates as far as you can see and the Nilgiri tahr of Eravikulam — Kerala's favourite hill station is just four hours from Kochi.
Highlights: Waterfalls, Tea gardens, Mattupetty Dam, Eravikulam Park
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:30 AM — Pickup & drive up: From your door, hotel, Ernakulam South, Vyttila or the airport; about 130 km on NH 85 via Kothamangalam, roughly 4 hours.
Day 1 · 9:30 AM — Cheeyappara & Valara falls: Roadside waterfalls in the Neriamangalam forest — a short photo stop. (Fullest in the monsoon)
Day 1 · midday — Tea Museum: How tea goes from leaf to cup, at Nullatanni. Lunch in Munnar town. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
Day 1 · afternoon — Mattupetty Dam & Echo Point: Lake views and optional boating on the Top Station road. Overnight in Munnar. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Eravikulam National Park: Park buses take you up Rajamala to see the Nilgiri tahr. (Tickets online · closed ~Feb–Mar)
Day 2 · ~6 PM — Drive home: Leave after lunch; back at your door in Kochi by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🐐 Eravikulam: Tickets are sold online in time slots — book a few days ahead; we can help. Closed for the tahr calving season, usually February–March; then we go to Top Station instead.
🍃 Tea & spices: Tea estates are private land — photograph from the roadside. Spice gardens at Pallivasal and Kallar are optional, paid direct.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel; Munnar town, Pothamedu and Chithirapuram are popular. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🧥 Weather & roads: Cool mornings, cold in December–January — bring a layer. In heavy-rain alerts hill roads can close at night — we plan to be off the ghat before dark.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; All Munnar sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Park, museum and boating fees; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Warm jacket; Walking shoes; Motion sickness tablets; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Thekkady spice & wildlife
Description: Walk a cardamom and pepper plantation, catch a Kathakali or Kalaripayattu show, and take the morning boat into the Periyar Tiger Reserve — about five hours from Kochi.
Highlights: Periyar boat cruise, Spice plantations, Kathakali show, Chellarkovil view
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door, hotel, Ernakulam South, Vyttila or the airport; about 175 km via Pala and the Kuttikkanam ghat, roughly 5–6 hours.
Day 1 · afternoon — Spice plantation tour: Cardamom, pepper, cinnamon and coffee with a local guide. (Paid direct)
Day 1 · evening — Kathakali or Kalaripayattu: Kerala's classical dance-drama or martial art at a Kumily theatre. Overnight in Thekkady. (Optional, paid direct)
Day 2 · 7:30 AM — Periyar Lake boat cruise: The first sailing — the best time to see elephants, gaur and deer at the water's edge. (Limited seats · tickets in advance)
Day 2 · late morning — Chellarkovil viewpoint: A cliff-edge view over the Cumbum valley and Tamil Nadu plains.
Day 2 · ~7 PM — Drive home: Down the ghat after lunch; back at your door in Kochi by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🛶 Periyar boating: Only a few sailings a day with limited seats — we help you book tickets in advance. Animal sightings are never guaranteed; boats stop in storms.
🌿 Spice shopping: Buy from plantations or fixed-price shops in Kumily. Leeches on plantation paths in the wet season — wear socks.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel in Kumily or on Thekkady Road. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🛣️ The drive: Ghat road after Mundakayam — carry motion sickness tablets if needed. Cool nights in Thekkady; pleasant all year.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; All Thekkady sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Boat, plantation and show tickets; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Light jacket; Walking shoes; Binoculars; Cash for tickets

Headline: Vagamon pine & meadows
Description: A long private day in Kerala's quiet hills: misty pine forest, rolling green meadows, the Kurisumala skyline and late-afternoon views from Thangalpara, about three hours from Kochi.
Highlights: Pine forest, Meadows & lake, Paragliding (opt.), Thangalpara views
Itinerary:
6:00 AM — Pickup: From your door — home, hotel, Ernakulam South, Vyttila or Cochin Airport. Breakfast at Thodupuzha.
9:30 AM — Pine forest: Walk under tall pines on the slopes just outside Vagamon town. (Entry own expense)
11:00 AM — Vagamon meadows & lake: Rolling grass hills with the Kurisumala view, then the calm lake ringed by tea. Lunch in town.
2:00 PM — Adventure park, Kolahalamedu: Paragliding in season and the glass bridge, when open. (Paid direct · operators confirm)
4:00 PM — Thangalpara: Hilltop rocks and a shrine with sweeping views over the valleys. (Easy uphill walk)
9:00 PM — Drop-off: Down via Erattupetta and Pala, back to your door in Kochi.
Good_To_Know:
🪂 Paragliding & glass bridge: Paragliding runs in season and only when the weather allows; pay the operator directly. The glass bridge has been closed for repairs — we confirm if it's open before your trip.
🌧️ Weather: Mist rolls in most afternoons; grass slopes are slippery after rain. Best from September to May; heavy-rain alerts can close viewpoints.
⏱️ A long day: About 3 hours each way on narrow hill roads. Prefer a slower pace? Ask us for a 2-day trip with a night in Vagamon.
👟 Walking: Meadows, pine forest and Thangalpara involve short uphill walks. Elderly guests can enjoy most views close to the road.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver; All Vagamon sightseeing drives; Driver bata; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Meals; Entry, paragliding and park tickets; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Light jacket; Walking shoes with grip; Raincoat or umbrella; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Houseboat a night afloat
Description: Drive from Kochi to Alappuzha, board a houseboat by noon and drift through Kuttanad's canals and paddy fields, with a night on the water and a beach stop on the way home.
Highlights: Night on a houseboat, Kuttanad canals, Meals on board, Marari beach (opt.)
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 9:30 AM — Pickup: From your door — home, hotel, Ernakulam South, Vyttila or Cochin Airport.
Day 1 · 10:00 AM — Drive to Alappuzha: About 55 km on NH 66 via Aroor and Cherthala, roughly 1.5–2 hours.
Day 1 · 12 noon — Board your houseboat: Cruise the backwaters with lunch, dinner and breakfast cooked on board. Overnight on the boat. (Houseboat booked by you · paid direct)
Day 2 · 9:00 AM — Check-out at the jetty: Your driver meets you at the boarding point with the vehicle.
Day 2 · 10:00 AM — Alappuzha or Marari beach: Optional — the old pier and lighthouse, or quiet Marari on the way home. (No swimming in rough sea)
Day 2 · ~1:30 PM — Home: Back to your door in Kochi.
Good_To_Know:
🚤 Booking the houseboat: You book and pay the houseboat directly; we can share contacts of licensed operators we trust. Check-in is usually around noon, check-out about 9 AM.
🛏️ On board: Boats stop cruising by early evening and anchor for the night. Ask the operator about AC hours, menus and life jackets.
🚗 Your driver: The vehicle stays with the driver in Alappuzha overnight. His night allowance is in our price.
🌧️ Season: Best from September to March; peak Dec–Jan — book early. In heavy rain, cruise routes may be shortened.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; Kochi ⇄ Alappuzha jetty drives; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Houseboat (paid direct); Meals off the boat; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Swimwear and a change of clothes; Mosquito repellent; Sunscreen and hat; ID for the houseboat check-in

Headline: Kerala classic circuit
Description: The classic Kerala holiday from Kochi: two nights in Munnar's tea hills, spice and wildlife in Thekkady, a night on the Alappuzha backwaters and a drop at the airport.
Highlights: Munnar tea hills, Periyar boating, Spice gardens, Houseboat night
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:30 AM — Kochi to Munnar: From your door, hotel or Cochin Airport; about 130 km past the Cheeyappara falls. Tea Museum in the afternoon. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 — Munnar sightseeing: Eravikulam Park, Mattupetty Dam, Echo Point and Top Station. (Entry fees paid direct)
Day 3 · morning — Munnar to Thekkady: About 110 km through cardamom hills; spice plantation walk.
Day 3 · 3:30 PM — Periyar Lake cruise: The afternoon sailing into the tiger reserve, then an optional Kathakali show. (Tickets paid direct · book early)
Day 4 — Thekkady to Alappuzha: About 160 km; board your houseboat around noon for a night on the backwaters. (Houseboat booked by you)
Day 5 · late morning — Kochi or Cochin Airport: About 60–85 km; drop at your door or in time for an afternoon flight.
Good_To_Know:
🚤 Houseboats: Book a licensed houseboat early for December–January. Check-in is usually around noon, check-out about 9 AM next day.
🐐 Eravikulam & Periyar: Eravikulam closes for tahr calving around Feb–Mar; book online slots ahead. Periyar boats have limited seats — we help you book.
🏨 Your stays: You book hotels in Munnar and Thekkady, and the houseboat. Your driver's bata and night allowances are in our price.
✈️ Flying out?: On Day 5 we can drop you at Cochin Airport for a flight from about 2 PM. Want more time? Add a night anywhere — ask us.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 5 days; All sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowances; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Hotels and houseboat; Meals; Entry, boat and show tickets; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Warm layer for Munnar; Walking shoes; Mosquito repellent; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Wayanad caves & forests
Description: Up the nine hairpins of the Thamarassery ghat to Kerala's green north: forest lakes, the country's largest earth dam and Edakkal's ancient carvings — your own vehicle and driver.
Highlights: Edakkal Caves, Banasura Dam, Pookode Lake, Thamarassery ghat
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive to Wayanad: From your door in Kochi — about 270 km via Thrissur, Kozhikode and the Thamarassery ghat, roughly 8 hours with breaks. (Stay booked by you)
Day 1 · afternoon — Lakkidi viewpoint & Pookode Lake: The view back down the ghat, then a forest lake right on the way in. (Boating optional, paid direct)
Day 2 · morning — Edakkal Caves: A short, steep climb to caves with prehistoric rock carvings. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
Day 2 · afternoon — Banasura Sagar Dam: India's largest earth dam, with green islands in the reservoir. (Entry & boating own expense)
Day 2 · or swap in — Chembra, Soochipara or Kuruva: A peak trek, a forest waterfall or bamboo-raft river islands — pick one. (Seasonal · we check if open)
Day 3 — Drive home: Leave after breakfast; back at your door in Kochi by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🪨 Edakkal Caves: Closed on Mondays — we plan around it. The climb is steep: not ideal for elders or small children.
🌧️ Seasonal spots: Kuruva Island closes in the monsoon and has a daily visitor cap; treks and falls can shut after heavy rain. We check on the day and swap stops.
🏨 Your stay: You book your resort or homestay; Kalpetta and Vythiri are central. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
⛰️ The ghat: Thamarassery ghat jams on weekends and holidays. We start early both ways to beat the queues.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 3 days; All Wayanad sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowances; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry, boating and trek fees; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Trekking shoes; Raincoat; Light jacket; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Ooty queen of hills
Description: The Nilgiris' classic hill stations: gardens, a lake and the highest peak in Ooty, tea country in Coonoor, and the famous toy train — your vehicle, your pace.
Highlights: Botanical Garden, Doddabetta Peak, Coonoor tea, Toy train (opt.)
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive to Ooty: From your door in Kochi — about 285 km via Palakkad, Coimbatore, Mettupalayam and the Coonoor ghat, roughly 8–9 hours. (Stay booked by you)
Day 1 · evening — Ooty Lake: An easy first evening: a walk or a boat on the lake. (Boating optional, paid direct)
Day 2 · morning — Botanical Garden & Doddabetta: Ooty's 1840s gardens, then the highest point in the Nilgiris. (Entry own expense)
Day 2 · afternoon — Coonoor — Sim's Park & Dolphin's Nose: Tea country, a hillside garden and a famous valley lookout.
Day 2 · optional — Nilgiri Mountain Railway: Ride the UNESCO-listed toy train between Ooty and Coonoor; we meet you at the other end. (Tickets in advance · paid direct)
Day 3 — Drive home: Leave after breakfast; back at your door in Kochi by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🎫 Nilgiris e-pass: Every vehicle entering the Nilgiris needs a Tamil Nadu e-pass — we apply for it. Single-use plastic is banned: carry refillable steel bottles.
🪪 Tamil Nadu entry: Ooty is in Tamil Nadu: interstate permit, border tax and green fee are billed at actual cost. We re-check entry rules before you travel.
🚂 Toy train: Seats sell out — book on IRCTC well before your trip. Timings change; we confirm them with you.
🧥 Weather: Cold nights all year — bring warm clothes. The ghat has many hairpins; carry motion sickness tablets.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 3 days; Ooty and Coonoor sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowances; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry, boating and toy train tickets; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Warm jacket; Photo ID; Refillable water bottle; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Kodaikanal princess of hills
Description: A star-shaped lake, cliff-edge walks and pillar rocks in the Palani hills — up the ghat from Palani to Tamil Nadu's cool retreat, with your own vehicle and driver.
Highlights: Kodai Lake, Coaker's Walk, Pillar Rocks, Pine forest
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive to Kodaikanal: From your door in Kochi — about 310 km via Palakkad, Pollachi, Palani and the Kodai ghat, roughly 9 hours. (Stay booked by you)
Day 1 · evening — Kodai Lake: A walk, a cycle or a boat round the star-shaped lake. (Boating paid direct)
Day 2 · morning — Coaker's Walk & Bryant Park: A cliff-edge path with views to the plains, then the gardens. (Entry own expense)
Day 2 · afternoon — Pillar Rocks, pine forest & Guna Caves viewpoint: Granite pillars, tall pines and the famous caves lookout. (Entry own expense)
Day 3 — Drive home: Leave after breakfast; back at your door in Kochi by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🎫 Kodaikanal e-pass: Tourist vehicles need a Tamil Nadu e-pass for Kodaikanal — we apply for it. Plastic is restricted: carry refillable bottles.
🪪 Tamil Nadu entry: Interstate permit, border tax and green fee are billed at actual cost. We re-check entry rules before you travel.
🌫️ Viewpoints: Mist can hide Pillar Rocks and Coaker's Walk — mornings are usually clearer. We reorder stops for the best views.
🧥 Weather: Cool all year, cold at night — bring warm layers. The ghat is winding: carry motion sickness tablets.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 3 days; Kodaikanal sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowances; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry and boating fees; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Warm jacket; Photo ID; Walking shoes; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Mysore city of palaces
Description: Up the Thamarassery ghat to Wayanad, through the Bandipur forest to Mysore's palace, Chamundi Hill, Brindavan and Srirangapatna — a royal road trip in your own vehicle.
Highlights: Mysore Palace, Brindavan Gardens, Bandipur forest, Chamundi Hill
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive to Wayanad: From your door in Kochi — about 270 km via Thrissur, Kozhikode and the Thamarassery ghat. Overnight in Wayanad. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Wayanad to Mysore via Bandipur: About 140 km through Muthanga and Bandipur forests — watch for deer and elephants. (Forest road closed at night)
Day 2 · evening — Srirangapatna & Brindavan Gardens: Tipu Sultan's island fort, then the gardens and musical fountain below KRS dam. (Entry own expense)
Day 3 · morning — Mysore Palace: The Wodeyars' palace of stained glass, mirrors and carved doors. (Entry own expense)
Day 3 · afternoon — Chamundi Hill & the lit-up palace: The hilltop temple and city view; the palace lights up on Sunday and holiday evenings. (Illumination Sun & holidays)
Day 4 · 6:00 AM — Long drive home: About 410 km via Gundlupet, Wayanad and Kozhikode; back in Kochi by night.
Good_To_Know:
🏰 Mysore Palace: Plan a Sunday or public holiday for the evening illumination. Shoes are removed inside — carry socks.
🪪 Karnataka entry: Mysore is in Karnataka: interstate permit, border tax and tolls are billed at actual cost. We re-check entry rules before you travel.
🐘 Bandipur road: The forest stretch is closed to traffic from 9 PM to 6 AM — we cross in daylight. No stopping or feeding animals inside the forest.
🏨 Your stays: You book one night in Wayanad and two in Mysore. Your driver's night allowances are in our price.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 4 days; All Mysore and Wayanad sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowances; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotels; Meals; Palace, garden and entry fees; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Photo ID; Socks for the palace; Light jacket; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Varkala & Trivandrum
Description: Red cliffs over the Arabian Sea and a Varkala sunset, then Trivandrum's great Padmanabhaswamy temple and the Napier Museum — or an afternoon at Kovalam.
Highlights: Varkala cliff, Cliff-top sunset, Padmanabhaswamy, Napier or Kovalam
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 7:00 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door in Kochi. About 170 km on NH 66 via Alappuzha and Kollam, 4–5 hours.
Day 1 · afternoon — Varkala Cliff & Papanasam Beach: Cliff-top walk and cafés, then steps down to the beach — strong currents. (Swim only at flagged spots)
Day 1 · ~5 PM — Janardana Swamy Temple: The ancient Vishnu temple on the hill above Papanasam. (Dress code · Hindus only inside)
Day 1 · sunset — Sunset on the cliff: Golden hour from the North Cliff. Overnight in Varkala. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · 8:30 AM — Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple: About 50 km to Trivandrum for morning darshan at the great Vishnu temple. (Strict dress code · Hindus only)
Day 2 · late morning — Napier Museum or Kovalam: Art and history in the Museum gardens — or a beach lunch at Kovalam. (Museum closed Mondays · entry own expense)
Day 2 · ~8 PM — Home or airport: About 210 km back to your door in Kochi — or a drop at Trivandrum Airport.
Good_To_Know:
🌊 Beach safety: Varkala's sea has strong currents and rip tides — swim only between lifeguard flags. No sea bathing in the monsoon (June–September); cliff paths are slippery after rain.
🛕 Temple rules: Padmanabhaswamy: Hindus only. Men in mundu, no shirt; women in saree or long skirt — mundus can be hired at the gate. Phones and cameras are not allowed inside.
🗓️ Closing days: Napier Museum is closed on Mondays and opens only at 1 PM on Wednesdays — on those days we head to Kovalam. The temple closes for a few hours at midday.
🏨 Stay & flights: You book your Varkala stay; North Cliff is the liveliest area. Flying out? End Day 2 at Trivandrum Airport — tell us your flight time.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; Varkala & Trivandrum sightseeing; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry fees and offerings; Tolls and parking

Headline: Kanyakumari land's end
Description: India's southern tip: the wooden palace of the Travancore kings, a sunset and a sunrise where three seas meet, and a ferry to Vivekananda Rock and the Thiruvalluvar statue.
Highlights: Sunrise & sunset, Vivekananda Rock, Glass bridge, Padmanabhapuram
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 5:30 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door in Kochi. About 300 km on NH 66 via Trivandrum, 7–8 hours with breaks.
Day 1 · 2:00 PM — Padmanabhapuram Palace: The Travancore kings' carved wooden palace at Thuckalay, on the way. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
Day 1 · evening — Sunset at Kanyakumari: Watch the sun go down at the tip of India. Overnight in Kanyakumari. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · ~6 AM — Sunrise over three seas: The famous sunrise from the shore by the temple.
Day 2 · 8:00 AM — Vivekananda Rock & Thiruvalluvar statue: Government ferry to the rock memorial; a glass bridge links it to the statue. (Ferry paid direct · go early)
Day 2 · late morning — Kumari Amman Temple: The ancient shore temple of the virgin goddess. (Men remove shirts · dress code)
Day 2 · ~9 PM — Home: About 300 km back to Kochi — Suchindram temple on the way if you wish.
Good_To_Know:
🛂 Tamil Nadu entry: Kanyakumari is in Tamil Nadu: interstate permit, border tax and tolls are billed at actual cost. We arrange the permit before your trip.
⛴️ The Rock ferry: Government ferries run from about 8 AM to 4 PM; queues grow after 9 — go early. Tickets paid direct; ferries pause when the sea is rough.
🛕 Palace & temple: Padmanabhapuram Palace is closed on Mondays — on a Monday we visit Suchindram instead. Kumari Amman: men remove shirts; modest dress for all.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel; sea-view rooms near the sunrise point fill fast. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.

Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Ferry, palace and temple tickets; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals

Headline: Palakkad & Nelliyampathy
Description: Tipu Sultan's fort and the Malampuzha gardens on day one, then ten hairpins up to Nelliyampathy's orange farms, tea estates and cliff-top views on day two.
Highlights: Palakkad Fort, Malampuzha gardens, Seethargundu view, Orange farms
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:30 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door, hotel, Ernakulam South, Vyttila or the airport; about 150 km on NH 544 via Thrissur, roughly 4 hours.
Day 1 · late morning — Palakkad Fort: Tipu Sultan's 18th-century granite fort in the heart of town, with its moat and ramparts. (Open ≈8 AM–6 PM)
Day 1 · evening — Malampuzha Dam & gardens: Landscaped gardens below the dam, the ropeway and an evening stroll. Overnight in Palakkad. (Entry own expense · stay booked by you)
Day 2 · 7:00 AM — Up to Nelliyampathy: Via Nenmara and Pothundy dam, then ten hairpins through the forest to Kaikatty. (Forest check post on the way)
Day 2 · morning — Seethargundu & orange farm: Cliff-top views over the Kollengode plains, Kesavanpara, the government orange farm and tea estates. Lunch in the hills. (Short walks)
Day 2 · ~7:30 PM — Drive home: Down the ghat by mid-afternoon; back at your door in Kochi by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🛣️ Nelliyampathy ghat: About 10 hairpins between Pothundy and Kaikatty — carry motion sickness tablets if needed. Vehicles are logged at the forest check post; we go up early and come down before dark.
⛲ Malampuzha: The gardens are best in the late afternoon and evening. Ropeway, boating and snake park are optional, paid direct.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel in Palakkad town or near Malampuzha. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🌧️ Weather: Best from September to February; cool mornings in the hills. Heavy monsoon rain can bring landslips on the ghat — we re-check the day before.

Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Fort, garden and ropeway fees; Tolls and parking

Headline: Sabarimala pilgrimage
Duration: 1 long day · set by your slot
Description: Your own vehicle from Kochi to Nilakkal base camp for the 2026-27 Mandala–Makaravilakku season, with an Erumely stop if you wish — the driver waits to bring you home.
Highlights: Virtual Queue slot, Erumely Petta Thullal, Nilakkal base camp, Door to door
Itinerary:
≈3:30 AM — Pickup: From your door — home, hotel, Ernakulam South, Vyttila or Cochin Airport. (Example: 10 AM slot)
On the road — Via Kottayam & Ponkunnam: About 150 km (or via Muvattupuzha and Pala), with a tea break.
≈6:30 AM — Erumely (optional): Petta Thullal at the Petta Sastha temple and a visit to Vavar Palli. (Tell us when booking)
≈8:30 AM — Nilakkal base camp: Private vehicles stop here; KSRTC chain buses take you on to Pampa. (Bus fare paid direct)
Day — Pampa, the climb & darshan: About 5 km uphill on foot to Sannidhanam, darshan, and the walk back. (Virtual Queue booked by you)
≈Midnight — Home: Your driver waits at Nilakkal and brings you home the same night.
Good_To_Know:
📱 Virtual Queue: Book your darshan slot yourself at sabarimalaonline.org; carry the QR coupon and the same photo ID. Spot-booking counters are limited — don't count on them.
🅿️ Nilakkal & Pampa: Private vehicles are not allowed to Pampa — KSRTC chain buses run from Nilakkal. Save your driver's number and the parking block.
🗓️ Season 2026-27: The temple opens on 16 Nov 2026; Mandala Pooja is on 27 Dec; Makaravilakku in mid-January 2027. Peak days bring police holds and long queues — we re-confirm before you travel.
❤️ The climb: About 5 km of steep forest path — go slow; medical centres with oxygen line the route. Elderly pilgrims and heart patients: check with your doctor first.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for the day; Erumely stop on request; Driver bata; No waiting charges at Nilakkal
Exclusions: KSRTC Nilakkal–Pampa bus; Meals and offerings; Virtual Queue booking (done by you); Tolls and parking

Headline: Kollam lake, fort & sea
Description: Kollam's old port town in one easy day: Portuguese fort ruins, the striped Thangassery lighthouse, a boat on Ashtamudi lake, quiet Thirumullavaram and an evening on Kollam beach.
Highlights: Thangassery lighthouse, Portuguese fort ruins, Ashtamudi boat ride, Thirumullavaram beach
Itinerary:
9:00 AM — Pickup: Kollam Junction station · Kollam KSRTC bus station · Trivandrum Airport (on request) (Airport pickup from 7:15 AM)
9:30 AM — Thangassery fort & breakwater: Ruins of the 16th-century Portuguese fort, old Anglo-Indian lanes and the breakwater.
10:15 AM — Thangassery lighthouse: Climb the 1902 lighthouse for views over the coast and Kollam port. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
11:30 AM — Ashtamudi lake boat ride: Out on the lake to the Sambranikodi sandbar when boats run. Lunch in town after, own expense. (Paid direct · life jackets on)
2:45 PM — Thirumullavaram beach: A calmer beach north of town with a small seaside temple.
4:15 PM — Kollam beach: Evening breeze and fishing boats on Mahatma Gandhi beach. (Walk only · rough sea)
5:30 PM — Drop-off: Kollam Junction, KSRTC bus station, or your own stop in the city
Good_To_Know:
🗓️ Closing days: Thangassery lighthouse is closed on Mondays; that day we add Chinnakada clock tower and a cashew shop instead. Lighthouse hours are 10 AM–1 PM and 2–6 PM; we re-confirm before your trip.
🛶 The boat ride: Licensed operators only, with a life jacket for everyone. Paid direct at the counter. No boating in storms or high wind — we switch to a lakeside walk.
🌊 Beaches: Kollam and Thangassery seas are rough — walking only, no swimming. Thirumullavaram is calmer; swim only where lifeguards are on duty.
🥜 Cashew town: Kollam is India's cashew capital — ask for the government cashew outlet. Try karimeen or prawns at lunch.

Exclusions: Lunch; Boat ride and lighthouse entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)

Headline: Munroe island canals
Description: Glide by canoe through Munroe Island's palm-shaded canals in the cool of the morning, see village life on the Kallada river, then Sasthamkotta, Kerala's largest freshwater lake.
Highlights: Canoe through canals, Island village life, Sasthamkotta lake, Lakeside temple
Itinerary:
7:00 AM — Pickup: Kollam Junction station · Kollam KSRTC bus station · Trivandrum Airport (on request) (Airport pickup on request)
7:45 AM — Munroe Island canoe ride: A country canoe poled through narrow canals past coir work, duck pens and prawn ponds. (Paid direct · about 2 hrs)
10:00 AM — Village breakfast & walk: Kerala breakfast at a homestay or tea shop, own expense, then a short walk on the island.
11:15 AM — Sasthamkotta temple: The lakeside Dharma Sastha temple, known for its monkeys. (Dress code · temple's entry rules)
11:45 AM — Sasthamkotta lake: Kerala's largest freshwater lake, a Ramsar wetland. Lunch nearby, own expense. (No swimming)
2:30 PM — Drop-off: Kollam Junction, KSRTC bus station, or your own stop in the city
Good_To_Know:
🛶 The canoe ride: Run by local canoe operators and paid direct; mornings are cooler and calmer. Low bridges over the canals — stay seated, hands inside the canoe.
🌧️ Weather & water: After very heavy rain or at high tide some canals close; the boatman picks a safe route. Little shade on the water — bring a hat and sunscreen.
🛕 Sasthamkotta: Dress modestly; entry rules inside are set by the temple. Monkeys snatch food and bags — keep them closed.
🌿 Village manners: Munroe is a living village — ask before photographing people or homes. No plastic in the canals, please.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Breakfast and lunch; Canoe ride; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Hat and sunscreen; Clothes that can get splashed; Cash for canoe & food; Insect repellent

Headline: Jatayu & Varkala cliff
Description: Ride the cable car up to the world's largest bird sculpture on the Chadayamangalam rock, then spend the afternoon on Varkala's red cliffs and Papanasam beach.
Highlights: Jatayu sculpture, Cable car ride, Varkala cliff, Papanasam beach
Itinerary:
8:00 AM — Pickup: Kollam Junction station · Kollam KSRTC bus station · Trivandrum Airport (on request) (Airport pickup on request)
9:30 AM — Jatayu Earth's Center: Cable car up the rock to the giant Jatayu sculpture, its museum and 360° views. (Tickets own expense)
11:15 AM — Adventure zone (optional): Zip-line, climbing or a short forest trek, run and priced by the park. (Paid to the park)
1:45 PM — Varkala North Cliff: Lunch at a cliff-top café, own expense, then the walk along the red cliffs. (Keep behind railings)
3:30 PM — Papanasam beach & temple: The sacred beach below the cliff and the ancient Janardhana Swamy temple. (Swim only near lifeguards)
6:30 PM — Drop-off: Kollam Junction, KSRTC bus station, or your own stop in the city
Good_To_Know:
🦅 Jatayu tickets: Cable-car tickets are sold by the park; on busy days book online the day before. Park timings can change — we re-confirm before your trip.
🧓 Elders & kids: The cable car takes you to the top — no climbing needed. The rock top is hot after 11 AM: carry water and a cap.
🌊 Varkala safety: Swim only between lifeguard flags; no sea bathing in the monsoon. Keep behind the cliff railings — the laterite edge crumbles.
👗 Temple & town: Dress modestly at the Janardhana temple; entry rules are the temple's. Beachwear on the beach only, not in town.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Jatayu tickets and activities; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Cap and sunscreen; Comfortable shoes; Swimwear & towel; Cash or card for tickets

Headline: Thenmala forest & falls
Description: A forest day on the Kollam–Shenkottai road: Punalur's old suspension bridge, Thenmala's eco-tourism zones and deer park, and the milky Palaruvi waterfall near Aryankavu.
Highlights: Butterfly park, Palaruvi Falls, Punalur bridge, Deer park
Itinerary:
7:00 AM — Pickup: Kollam Junction station · Kollam KSRTC bus station · Trivandrum Airport (on request) (Airport pickup on request)
8:15 AM — Punalur suspension bridge: A short stop at the 1877 bridge over the Kallada river. Breakfast in Punalur, own expense.
9:30 AM — Thenmala eco-tourism: Butterfly park, elevated forest walkway, suspension bridge and the deer rehabilitation centre. (Tickets own expense)
1:00 PM — Palaruvi Waterfalls: Lunch at Thenmala first, own expense; then the 300-ft 'river of milk' near Aryankavu. (Forest entry · open till 4 PM)
3:45 PM — Thenmala dam: Views over the Parappar reservoir on the way back.
6:30 PM — Drop-off: Kollam Junction, KSRTC bus station, or your own stop in the city

💧 Palaruvi: Forest department entry, open about 8 AM–4 PM; best after the monsoon. Bathing only where staff allow; closed in very heavy rain.
🌳 Forest rules: No plastic, no feeding animals. Elephants sometimes cross near Aryankavu — everyone stays inside if we stop.
🛣️ The drive: About 1 h 45 each way on NH 744 via Kottarakkara and Punalur. Lorries to Tamil Nadu use this road — we drive steady, not fast.

Headline: Trivandrum in a day
Description: The capital in one easy day from Kollam: morning darshan at the great Padmanabhaswamy temple, the Napier Museum and its gardens, then lunch and the beaches of Kovalam.
Highlights: Padmanabhaswamy, Napier Museum, Kovalam beach, Vizhinjam lighthouse
Itinerary:
6:30 AM — Pickup: Kollam Junction station · Kollam KSRTC bus station · Trivandrum Airport (on request) (Airport guests join in Trivandrum)
8:30 AM — Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple: Morning darshan at the great Vishnu temple in East Fort. Non-Hindu guests see the gopuram and the Fort area. (Hindus only · strict dress code)
10:30 AM — Napier Museum & gardens: The 1880 Indo-Saracenic museum, Sree Chitra Art Gallery (Raja Ravi Varma) and the zoo, all in one compound. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
1:15 PM — Kovalam: lunch & beach: Seafood lunch by the sea (own expense), then Lighthouse and Hawa beaches. (Swim only at lifeguard flags)
3:45 PM — Vizhinjam lighthouse: Climb the red-and-white tower above Lighthouse Beach for views down the coast. (Tower: check timings)
7:00 PM — Drop-off: Kollam Junction, KSRTC bus station, or your own stop in the city

🌊 Beach safety: Kovalam has strong currents — swim only between the lifeguard flags. No sea bathing at all in the monsoon months.
✈️ Flying in or out?: Landing at Trivandrum? Join the tour in the city in the morning — ask us. Or end your day at Trivandrum Airport for an evening flight.

Exclusions: Lunch; Museum, zoo and lighthouse entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)

Headline: Alappuzha & Amritapuri
Description: A calm morning at Amritapuri, Mata Amritanandamayi's ashram between backwater and sea, then a shikara ride through Alappuzha's canals and an afternoon on the beach.
Highlights: Amritapuri ashram, Shikara canal ride, Alappuzha beach, 1862 lighthouse

7:00 AM — Pickup: Kollam Junction station · Kollam KSRTC bus station · Trivandrum Airport (on request)
8:00 AM — Amritapuri ashram: Walk the ashram at Vallikavu: the temple, the meditation halls and the strip between the backwater and the sea. (Modest dress · quiet please)
10:45 AM — Shikara canal ride: About 2 hours on Punnamada lake, narrow village canals and paddy fields. (Boat paid direct)
1:00 PM — Lunch & Alappuzha beach: Karimeen lunch in town (own expense), then the old pier and promenade. (No swimming here)

6:30 PM — Drop-off: Kollam Junction, KSRTC bus station, or your own stop in the city

Headline: Ponmudi hills & mist
Description: Your own vehicle for a cool day in the hills: a river stop at Kallar, 22 hairpin bends through forest and tea, and misty ridges at Ponmudi top — about 2.5 hours from Kollam.
Highlights: 22 hairpin bends, Misty viewpoints, Tea slopes, Kallar river
Itinerary:
6:30 AM — Pickup: From your door, hotel, Kollam Junction or the KSRTC stand; via Kilimanoor and Palode, breakfast on the way.
9:15 AM — Kallar riverside & Golden Valley: A cool river stop at the foot of the hills, by the forest check post. (Photos only · no bathing)
9:45 AM — The 22 hairpin bends: The climb through forest and tea to about 1,100 m, with stops at safe viewpoints.
10:45 AM — Ponmudi top & viewpoints: Grassy ridges, mist and views over the Western Ghats. Lunch near the top, own expense. (Entry own expense)
2:30 PM — Meenmutty Falls (if open): A forest walk with a guide to a waterfall near Kallar. (Seasonal · forest dept. permit)
7:00 PM — Drop-off: Back to your door or any stop in Kollam.

🌫️ Weather: Cool and misty most of the year — bring a light jacket. In heavy rain the forest department can close Ponmudi; we re-confirm the day before.
🛣️ Hairpin road: 22 bends on the climb — carry motion sickness tablets if needed. Your driver stops on the way so nobody feels rushed.
💧 Meenmutty Falls: Open in season only, with a forest guide and a short walk. If it's closed, you get more time at the top instead.
🍃 Protected forest: Most tea land is private — photograph from paths and roadsides. No plastic and no bathing in the river: Ponmudi is a protected forest area.

Headline: Munnar tea hills
Description: Waterfalls on the climb, tea estates as far as you can see and the Nilgiri tahr of Eravikulam — Kerala's favourite hill station, up the MC Road from Kollam.
Highlights: Waterfalls, Tea gardens, Eravikulam Park, Mattupetty Dam
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 5:30 AM — Pickup & drive up: From your door, hotel, Kollam Junction or the KSRTC stand; about 250 km via Kottayam, Muvattupuzha and Kothamangalam, roughly 7 hours with breaks.
Day 1 · 11:15 AM — Cheeyappara & Valara falls: Roadside waterfalls in the Neriamangalam forest — a short photo stop. (Fullest in the monsoon)
Day 1 · afternoon — Tea Museum: How tea goes from leaf to cup, at Nullatanni. Lunch in Munnar town; overnight in Munnar. (Closed Mondays · stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Eravikulam National Park: Park buses take you up Rajamala to see the Nilgiri tahr. (Tickets online · closed ~Feb–Mar)
Day 2 · late morning — Mattupetty Dam & Echo Point: Lake views and optional boating on the Top Station road. (Boating paid direct)

🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel; Munnar town, Pothamedu and Chithirapuram are popular. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🧥 Weather & roads: Cool mornings, cold in December–January — bring a layer. In heavy-rain alerts hill roads can close at night — we plan to be off the ghat before dark.

Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Park, museum and boating fees; Tolls and parking

Headline: Thekkady spice & wildlife
Description: Walk a cardamom and pepper plantation, catch a Kathakali or Kalaripayattu show, and take the morning boat into the Periyar Tiger Reserve — about five hours from Kollam.
Highlights: Periyar boat cruise, Spice plantations, Kathakali show, Chellarkovil view
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door, hotel, Kollam Junction or the KSRTC stand; about 175 km via Pathanamthitta, Erumely and the Kuttikkanam ghat, roughly 5–6 hours.
Day 1 · afternoon — Spice plantation tour: Cardamom, pepper, cinnamon and coffee with a local guide. (Paid direct)
Day 1 · evening — Kathakali or Kalaripayattu: Kerala's classical dance-drama or martial art at a Kumily theatre. Overnight in Thekkady. (Optional, paid direct)
Day 2 · 7:30 AM — Periyar Lake boat cruise: The first sailing — the best time to see elephants, gaur and deer at the water's edge. (Limited seats · tickets in advance)
Day 2 · late morning — Chellarkovil viewpoint: A cliff-edge view over the Cumbum valley and Tamil Nadu plains.

🛶 Periyar boating: Only a few sailings a day with limited seats — we help you book tickets in advance. Animal sightings are never guaranteed; boats stop in storms.

🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel in Kumily or on Thekkady Road. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🛣️ The drive: Ghat road after Mundakayam — carry motion sickness tablets if needed. Cool nights in Thekkady; pleasant all year.

Headline: Kanyakumari land's end
Description: India's southern tip in one long private day from Kollam: the shore temple of the virgin goddess, a ferry to Vivekananda Rock, and the carved wooden palace of the Travancore kings.
Highlights: Kumari Amman, Vivekananda Rock, Glass bridge, Padmanabhapuram
Itinerary:
5:00 AM — Pickup: From your door, hotel, Kollam Junction or the KSRTC stand. About 165 km on NH 66 via the Trivandrum bypass; breakfast at Marthandam.
9:30 AM — Kumari Amman Temple: The ancient shore temple of the virgin goddess, where three seas meet. (Men remove shirts · closes ~12:15)
10:30 AM — Vivekananda Rock & Thiruvalluvar statue: Government ferry to the rock memorial; a glass bridge links it to the statue. Lunch in town after. (Ferry paid direct)
2:45 PM — Padmanabhapuram Palace: The Travancore kings' carved wooden palace at Thuckalay, on the way home. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
8:00 PM — Drop-off: Back to your door or any stop in Kollam.

⛴️ The Rock ferry: Government ferries run from about 8 AM to 4 PM; queues can take an hour. Tickets paid direct; ferries pause when the sea is rough.
🗓️ Mondays: Padmanabhapuram Palace is closed on Mondays. On a Monday we stop at Suchindram temple on the way in instead.
⏱️ A long day: About 4 hours each way — sunrise and sunset need a 2-day trip: ask us. Kumari Amman: men remove shirts; modest dress for all.

Exclusions: Meals; Ferry, palace and temple tickets; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals

Headline: Konni elephants & boats
Description: Meet the young elephants at Konni's 1942 timber elephant kraal, spin down the forest-lined Kallar river in a round bamboo coracle at Adavi, then visit the riverside forest shrine at Kalleli.

7:30 AM — Pickup: Pathanamthitta KSRTC stand · Thiruvalla station · Chengannur station (Thiruvalla 7:30 · Chengannur 7:50 · PTA 8:30)
9:00 AM — Konni Elephant Camp: The old Anakoodu timber kraal, the calves at feeding and bath time, and a small elephant museum. (Entry own expense)
11:00 AM — Adavi coracle ride: Round bamboo boats on the Kallar river through bamboo and forest. Lunch in Konni after, own expense. (Ride paid direct)

Headline: Aranmula heritage trail
Description: Old temples and older churches along the Pampa: Chengannur Mahadeva, Aranmula's snake-boat temple and its famous metal mirror, then the pilgrim churches of Parumala and Niranam.
Highlights: Aranmula temple, Metal mirror workshop, Chengannur Mahadeva, Parumala & Niranam
Itinerary:
7:00 AM — Pickup: Pathanamthitta KSRTC stand · Thiruvalla station · Chengannur station (PTA 7:00 · Thiruvalla 7:45 · Chengannur 8:05)
8:15 AM — Chengannur Mahadeva Temple: A grand Kerala temple of Shiva and Parvati, busiest at the morning poojas. (Dress code · see below)
9:40 AM — Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple: Krishna temple on the Pampa, home of the snake boats. (Morning only · dress code)
11:00 AM — Aranmula kannadi workshop: The metal mirror, cast and polished by hand. Lunch after, own expense. (Buying is optional)
2:00 PM — Parumala & Niranam churches: St Gregorios' tomb at Parumala, then Niranam's old church, linked by tradition to St Thomas. (Modest dress)
5:15 PM — Drop-off: Pathanamthitta, Thiruvalla, Chengannur, or your own stop on the way
Good_To_Know:
🛕 Temple rules: Most Kerala temples admit only Hindus inside; other guests see the gateway, pond and river from outside. Men: shirts off and dhoti or trousers; women: saree, churidar or long skirt. Footwear stays in the vehicle.
🪞 The Aranmula mirror: Made from a secret metal alloy, polished until the metal itself reflects — a GI-tagged craft. Genuine mirrors are costly: buy only from the workshop, with its certificate.
🚣 Festivals & crowds: Aug–Sept brings the Uthrattathi snake-boat race and Vallasadya feasts at Aranmula — ask us for dates. Parumala Perunnal (early Nov) draws huge crowds; we may change the order that week.
🚉 Pickup points: Pathanamthitta first, then Thiruvalla, then Chengannur — we share exact times the evening before. Drop-off at Thiruvalla, Chengannur, then Pathanamthitta, or your own stop on the way.

Headline: Waterfalls Perunthenaruvi
Description: Watch the Pampa spread wide and crash over a broad shelf of rock at Perunthenaruvi, visit Erumely's Vavar mosque and Sastha temple on the Sabarimala trail, then take tea by the river at Ranni.

Itinerary:

12:00 PM — Erumely: Vavar mosque and the Dharma Sastha temple, both visited by Sabarimala pilgrims. Lunch here, own expense. (Modest dress)

Headline: Alappuzha backwaters
Description: Cross Kuttanad's paddy country on the AC road, glide through Alappuzha's canals on a shikara, walk the old pier and 1862 lighthouse, then meet the stone Buddha of Karumadi.
