Headline: Gavi forest & dams
Description: A full private day through the Gavi rainforest: in at Angamoozhy, past the Sabarigiri dams and Gavi lake, out to Vandiperiyar's tea country and home over Kuttikkanam.
Highlights: Rainforest drive, Sabarigiri dams, Gavi lake boating, Tea-estate return
Itinerary:
6:00 AM — Pickup: From your door — home, hotel, Pathanamthitta KSRTC stand, or Thiruvalla / Chengannur station (earlier start). (Breakfast at Seethathode)
8:30 AM — Angamoozhy check post: Forest pass check at the Kochandi gate; the one-way forest road to Gavi starts here. (Online pass booked ahead)
9:30 AM — Moozhiyar, Kakki & Anathode: Dams and blue reservoirs of the Sabarigiri project in deep forest, watching for deer, birds and elephants. (Photos from the road only)
12:30 PM — Gavi lake: Lunch at Gavi, a boat ride on the lake and the cardamom-forest views. (Lunch and boating paid direct)
3:45 PM — Vallakkadavu & Vandiperiyar: Exit check post, then tea estates and a tea break at Vandiperiyar.
7:30 PM — Drop-off: Down the ghat via Kuttikkanam, Mundakayam, Erumely and Ranni to your door.
Good_To_Know:
🛂 Forest pass: Private vehicles need a Gavi pass booked online before the trip; numbers per day are limited. Entry at Angamoozhy is only in the morning window — that's why we start at 6:00 AM.
➡️ One-way road: Vehicles from Angamoozhy must exit at Vallakkadavu (Vandiperiyar) the same day — no U-turn. No stops off the road, no music, no plastic, no alcohol in the forest.
🗓️ Closures: Gavi closes for a few days around Makaravilakku (mid-January) and on heavy-rain alerts. We re-confirm the forest status the day before your trip.
📵 No signal: Mobile network is mostly absent between Angamoozhy and Gavi. Carry snacks, water and any medicines you need — shops are few.

Exclusions: Meals; Forest passes and boating; Tolls and parking

Headline: Vagamon pine & meadows
Description: A long private day in Kerala's quiet hills: misty pine forest, rolling green meadows, the Kurisumala skyline and late-afternoon views from Thangalpara, about three hours from Pathanamthitta.
Highlights: Pine forest, Meadows & lake, Paragliding (opt.), Thangalpara views
Itinerary:
6:30 AM — Pickup: From your door — home, hotel, Pathanamthitta, Thiruvalla or Chengannur. Breakfast at Kanjirappally.
9:45 AM — Pine forest: Walk under tall pines on the slopes just outside Vagamon town. (Entry own expense)
11:00 AM — Vagamon meadows & lake: Rolling grass hills with the Kurisumala view, then the calm lake ringed by tea. Lunch in town.
2:00 PM — Adventure park, Kolahalamedu: Paragliding in season and the glass bridge, when open. (Paid direct · operators confirm)
4:00 PM — Thangalpara: Hilltop rocks and a shrine with sweeping views over the valleys. (Easy uphill walk)
8:30 PM — Drop-off: Down via Erattupetta, Kanjirappally and Ranni, back to your door.
Good_To_Know:
🪂 Paragliding & glass bridge: Paragliding runs in season and only when the weather allows; pay the operator directly. The glass bridge has been closed for strengthening — we confirm if it's open before your trip.
🌧️ Weather: Mist rolls in most afternoons; grass slopes are slippery after rain. Best from September to May; heavy-rain alerts can close viewpoints.
⏱️ A long day: About 3 hours each way on narrow hill and estate roads. Prefer a slower pace? Ask us for a 2-day trip with a night in Vagamon.
👟 Walking: Meadows, pine forest and Thangalpara involve short uphill walks. Elderly guests can enjoy most views close to the road.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver; All Vagamon sightseeing drives; Driver bata; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Meals; Entry, paragliding and park tickets; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Light jacket; Walking shoes with grip; Raincoat or umbrella; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Kanyakumari land's end
Description: India's southern tip: the wooden palace of the Travancore kings, a sunset and a sunrise where three seas meet, and a ferry to Vivekananda Rock and the Thiruvalluvar statue.
Highlights: Sunrise & sunset, Vivekananda Rock, Glass bridge, Padmanabhapuram
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door, Pathanamthitta or Chengannur. About 210 km via Adoor, the MC Road and Trivandrum, 5–6 hours with breaks.
Day 1 · 11:15 AM — Padmanabhapuram Palace: The Travancore kings' carved wooden palace at Thuckalay, on the way. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
Day 1 · evening — Sunset at Kanyakumari: Watch the sun go down at the tip of India. Overnight in Kanyakumari. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · ~6 AM — Sunrise over three seas: The famous sunrise from the shore by the temple.
Day 2 · 8:00 AM — Vivekananda Rock & Thiruvalluvar statue: Government ferry to the rock memorial; a glass bridge links it to the statue. (Ferry paid direct · go early)
Day 2 · late morning — Kumari Amman Temple: The ancient shore temple of the virgin goddess. (Men remove shirts · dress code)
Day 2 · ~8 PM — Home: About 210 km back — Suchindram temple on the way if you wish.
Good_To_Know:
🛂 Tamil Nadu entry: Kanyakumari is in Tamil Nadu: interstate permit, border tax and tolls are billed at actual cost. We arrange the permit before your trip.
⛴️ The Rock ferry: Government ferries run from about 8 AM to 4 PM; queues grow after 9 — go early. Tickets paid direct; ferries pause when the sea is rough.
🛕 Palace & temple: Padmanabhapuram Palace is closed on Mondays — on a Monday we visit Suchindram instead. Kumari Amman: men remove shirts; modest dress for all.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel; sea-view rooms near the sunrise point fill fast. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; Palace, sunset & temple drives; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Ferry, palace and temple tickets; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Photo ID; Modest temple clothes; Hat and sunscreen; Cash for ferry and entry

Headline: Alappuzha canals
Description: The 'Venice of the East' in a day: a shikara through Kuttanad's canals, Mullakkal's temple street, old canal-side warehouses, the 1862 lighthouse and the old pier.
Highlights: Shikara canal ride, Kuttanad paddy views, 1862 lighthouse, Beach & old pier
Itinerary:
8:30 AM — Pickup: Alappuzha railway station · Alappuzha KSRTC bus station · your hotel in town (Hotel pickups in town)
9:00 AM — Mullakkal temple street: The town's busy temple and market street. (Modest dress · temple rules apply)
9:45 AM — Shikara through Kuttanad: About 3 hours over Punnamada lake into village canals and paddy fields. (Boat paid direct)
1:00 PM — Lunch & the old canals: Karimeen lunch (own expense), then old warehouses on the Vadai canal.
3:00 PM — Alappuzha lighthouse: The 1862 lighthouse — climb up for views over the town and coast. (Tower: check timings)
4:15 PM — Alappuzha beach & old pier: The long beach and the ruins of the 150-year-old pier. (No swimming here)
6:00 PM — Drop-off: Alappuzha station, KSRTC bus station, your hotel or houseboat jetty
Good_To_Know:
🛶 The boat ride: Shikaras are run by licensed operators near Finishing Point; the fare is paid direct to the operator. Life jackets for everyone; children always with an adult.
🗓️ Timings: The lighthouse tower usually opens in the morning and afternoon and may close on Mondays — then we see it from outside. Temples follow their own rules on dress and entry; we see them from outside if needed.
🌊 Beach safety: No swimming at Alappuzha beach — strong currents and old pier piles under the water. Paddle only at the edge, and never in the monsoon months.
🏨 Staying out of town?: We pick up from hotels and houseboat jetties in Alappuzha town. Staying at a resort further out? Ask us — a short extra drive may apply.

Exclusions: Shikara fare (paid direct); Lunch and lighthouse entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)

Headline: Kuttanad villages
Description: Into Kerala's rice bowl, where paddy grows below sea level: dyke roads through Kuttanad, an ancient basilica on the snake-boat river, Edathua's Gothic church and Thakazhi's home.
Highlights: Paddy below sea level, Champakulam basilica, Edathua church, Thakazhi's home
Itinerary:
8:00 AM — Pickup: Alappuzha railway station · Alappuzha KSRTC bus station · your hotel in town (Hotel pickups in town)
8:45 AM — Paddy below sea level: Mankombu's fields, farmed up to 2 m below sea level behind mud dykes. (Photo stop)
9:30 AM — Champakulam basilica: St Mary's, by tradition from AD 427, on the river of the Moolam snake-boat race. (Modest dress)
11:15 AM — Edathua St George's church: A tall Gothic church on the Pampa, a famous pilgrim centre. (Modest dress)
12:30 PM — Kuttanadan lunch: Duck roast, karimeen and Kerala meals at a village restaurant, own expense.
2:00 PM — Thakazhi museum: Home of Thakazhi Sivasankara Pillai, author of Chemmeen. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
4:30 PM — Drop-off: Alappuzha station, KSRTC bus station, your hotel or houseboat jetty
Good_To_Know:
🌾 Kuttanad: Kuttanad's below-sea-level farming is a UN FAO-recognised heritage system — paddy behind dykes, canals above the fields. Roads run on narrow dykes; we stop only at safe spots for photos.
⛪ Churches: Shoulders and knees covered; quiet during mass and prayers. On feast days and Sundays the churches are crowded — we keep the visit short.
🗓️ Mondays & rain: The Thakazhi museum is closed on Mondays — then we add time at Champakulam and the river bank. In heavy rain Kuttanad roads can flood; we change the route if needed.
🏨 Staying out of town?: We pick up from hotels and houseboat jetties in Alappuzha town. Staying at a resort further out? Ask us — a short extra drive may apply.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Museum entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Clothes covering shoulders and knees; Hat and sunscreen; Umbrella in the rains; Insect repellent

Headline: Krishna & Buddha
Description: Ambalappuzha's Krishna temple, the black-granite Karumadi Buddha and Krishnapuram Palace's giant mural, then home along the coast.
Highlights: Ambalappuzha temple, Karumadi Buddha, Gajendra Moksham mural, Coast lighthouse
Itinerary:
7:00 AM — Pickup: Alappuzha railway station · Alappuzha KSRTC bus station · your hotel in town
7:30 AM — Ambalappuzha Sri Krishna temple: Home of the famous palpayasam; breakfast nearby, own expense. (Temple dress code)
9:00 AM — Karumadi Kuttan: A centuries-old black-granite Buddha in a small shrine near Ambalappuzha.
10:30 AM — Krishnapuram Palace: 18th-century palace with the huge Gajendra Moksham mural; lunch after. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
2:00 PM — Valiyazheekal lighthouse: A 41 m lighthouse and the arch bridge over the estuary. (Tower: check timings)
3:45 PM — Thottappally: Where Kuttanad's rivers meet the sea: spillway and beach. (No swimming)
5:30 PM — Drop-off: Alappuzha station, KSRTC bus station, your hotel or houseboat jetty
Good_To_Know:
🛕 Temple visit: Men enter bare-chested in a mundu or dhoti; women in a saree, churidar or long skirt. Entry inside follows temple rules — guests who don't enter can see the temple pond and gateway.
🗓️ Closing days: Krishnapuram Palace is closed on Mondays and some public holidays — we don't run this tour on Mondays. Temple timings change on festival days; we re-confirm before your trip.
🌊 Beach safety: No swimming at Valiyazheekal or Thottappally — river mouths with strong currents. Stay off the breakwater rocks when waves are high.
🏨 Staying out of town?: We pick up from hotels and houseboat jetties in Alappuzha town. Staying at a resort further out? Ask us — a short extra drive may apply.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Breakfast and lunch; Palace and lighthouse entry, temple offerings; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Mundu / dhoti or saree for the temple; Hat and sunscreen; Cash for entry and offerings; Comfortable sandals

Headline: Marari & Arthunkal
Description: North up the coast from Alappuzha: palm-lined Marari beach, Arthunkal's Portuguese-era basilica and fishing beach, then the Thanneermukkom bund across Vembanad lake.
Highlights: Marari beach, Arthunkal basilica, Thanneermukkom bund, Vembanad lake views
Itinerary:
8:00 AM — Pickup: Alappuzha railway station · Alappuzha KSRTC bus station · your hotel in town (Hotel pickups in town)
8:45 AM — Marari beach: A quiet, palm-lined fishing-village beach, best in the morning. (Swim only at lifeguard flags)
10:45 AM — Arthunkal basilica & beach: St Andrew's Basilica (rebuilt 1584) and the fishing beach beside it. (Modest dress)
12:30 PM — Lunch in Cherthala: Kerala meals or seafood at a town restaurant, own expense.
2:00 PM — Thanneermukkom bund: The great salt-water barrier across Vembanad lake: wide views, fishing canoes.
3:30 PM — Muhamma lakeside: The lake shore drive back, with views to Pathiramanal island. (Photo stop)
5:00 PM — Drop-off: Alappuzha station, KSRTC bus station, your hotel or houseboat jetty
Good_To_Know:
🌊 Beach safety: At Marari, swim only near the lifeguards and where flags allow — never at red flags. No sea bathing at Arthunkal or anywhere in the monsoon months.
⛪ Arthunkal: Shoulders and knees covered inside the basilica; quiet during mass. The January feast brings huge crowds — on those days we keep the stop short.
🌞 Sun & sand: Little shade on the beaches — bring a hat, sunscreen and water. Carry a change of clothes if you plan to get wet at Marari.
🏨 Staying out of town?: Staying at a Marari resort? We can pick you up there on the way. Hotels and houseboat jetties in Alappuzha town are included.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Any boat rides (paid direct); Tolls and parking (private trips)

Headline: Kochi heritage in a day
Description: Five centuries of Kochi in a day from Alappuzha: Chinese fishing nets, India's oldest European church, a Dutch palace of murals, Jew Town and Marine Drive.
Highlights: Chinese fishing nets, St Francis Church, Dutch Palace murals, Jew Town
Itinerary:
7:30 AM — Pickup: Alappuzha railway station · Alappuzha KSRTC bus station · your hotel in town
9:30 AM — Fort Kochi: fishing nets & churches: Chinese fishing nets, St Francis Church (Vasco da Gama's first grave) and Santa Cruz Basilica. (Modest dress in the churches)
11:15 AM — Mattancherry Palace: The 'Dutch Palace' with its Ramayana murals and royal portraits. (Closed Fridays · entry own expense)
12:00 PM — Jew Town & Paradesi Synagogue: Antique shops, spice stores and the 1568 synagogue. Lunch here, own expense. (Synagogue closed Fri & Sat)
2:30 PM — Kerala Folklore Museum: Masks, costumes and carved wooden halls from across South India. (Entry own expense)
4:00 PM — Marine Drive: A walk on the backwater promenade before the drive home.
6:45 PM — Drop-off: Alappuzha station, KSRTC bus station, your hotel or houseboat jetty
Good_To_Know:
🗓️ Closing days: Mattancherry Palace is closed on Fridays; the synagogue on Fridays, Saturdays and Jewish holidays. On those days we swap in the Hill Palace Museum at Tripunithura — same price.
👗 What to wear: Shoulders and knees covered for the churches, synagogue and palace. No photos inside the synagogue or the palace galleries.
🚶 Walking: Fort Kochi and Jew Town are best on foot — about 3–4 km of easy walking in all. Wear comfortable shoes; lanes are uneven in places.
🚐 The drive: About 1 hr 45 min each way on NH 66 via Cherthala and Aroor. Evening traffic at Vyttila and Kundannoor can make the drop a little later.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Palace, synagogue and museum entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Comfortable walking shoes; Clothes covering shoulders and knees; Hat and sunscreen; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Munnar tea hills
Description: Waterfalls on the climb, tea estates as far as you can see and the Nilgiri tahr of Eravikulam — Kerala's favourite hill station, about five hours from Alappuzha.
Highlights: Waterfalls, Tea gardens, Mattupetty Dam, Eravikulam Park
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive up: From your door, hotel, houseboat jetty or Alappuzha station; about 175 km via Aroor and Kothamangalam, roughly 5–5.5 hours.
Day 1 · 10:00 AM — Cheeyappara & Valara falls: Roadside waterfalls in the Neriamangalam forest — a short photo stop. (Fullest in the monsoon)
Day 1 · afternoon — Tea Museum: Lunch in Munnar town, then how tea goes from leaf to cup at Nullatanni. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
Day 1 · evening — Mattupetty Dam & Echo Point: Lake views and optional boating on the Top Station road. Overnight in Munnar. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Eravikulam National Park: Park buses take you up Rajamala to see the Nilgiri tahr. (Tickets online · closed ~Feb–Mar)
Day 2 · ~7 PM — Drive home: Leave after lunch; back at your door in Alappuzha by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🐐 Eravikulam: Tickets are sold online in time slots — book a few days ahead; we can help. Closed for the tahr calving season, usually February–March; then we go to Top Station instead.
🍃 Tea & spices: Tea estates are private land — photograph from the roadside. Spice gardens at Pallivasal and Kallar are optional, paid direct.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel; Munnar town, Pothamedu and Chithirapuram are popular. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🧥 Weather & roads: Cool mornings, cold in December–January — bring a layer. In heavy-rain alerts hill roads can close at night — we plan to be off the ghat before dark.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; All Munnar sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Park, museum and boating fees; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Warm jacket; Walking shoes; Motion sickness tablets; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Thekkady spice & wildlife
Description: Walk a cardamom and pepper plantation, catch a Kathakali or Kalaripayattu show, and take the morning boat into the Periyar Tiger Reserve — about 4–5 hours from Alappuzha.
Highlights: Periyar boat cruise, Spice plantations, Kathakali show, Chellarkovil view
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door, hotel, houseboat jetty or Alappuzha station; about 140 km via Changanassery and the Kuttikkanam ghat, roughly 4–5 hours.
Day 1 · afternoon — Spice plantation tour: Cardamom, pepper, cinnamon and coffee with a local guide. (Paid direct)
Day 1 · evening — Kathakali or Kalaripayattu: Kerala's classical dance-drama or martial art at a Kumily theatre. Overnight in Thekkady. (Optional, paid direct)
Day 2 · 7:30 AM — Periyar Lake boat cruise: The first sailing — the best time to see elephants, gaur and deer at the water's edge. (Limited seats · tickets in advance)
Day 2 · late morning — Chellarkovil viewpoint: A cliff-edge view over the Cumbum valley and Tamil Nadu plains.
Day 2 · ~6:30 PM — Drive home: Down the ghat after lunch; back at your door in Alappuzha by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🛶 Periyar boating: Only a few sailings a day with limited seats — we help you book tickets in advance. Animal sightings are never guaranteed; boats stop in storms.
🌿 Spice shopping: Buy from plantations or fixed-price shops in Kumily. Leeches on plantation paths in the wet season — wear socks.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel in Kumily or on Thekkady Road. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🛣️ The drive: Ghat road after Mundakayam — carry motion sickness tablets if needed. The AC Road through Kuttanad can flood in heavy rain; we reroute if needed.

Headline: Varkala cliffs & sea
Description: Red laterite cliffs over the Arabian Sea, the old Janardana Swamy temple, Sree Narayana Guru's Sivagiri and a quiet sunset at Kappil, where the backwater meets the sea.
Highlights: Varkala cliff, Papanasam Beach, Sivagiri Mutt, Kappil sunset
Itinerary:
6:30 AM — Pickup: From your door — home, hotel, houseboat jetty or Alappuzha station. Breakfast at Kayamkulam on NH 66.
9:45 AM — Varkala Cliff & Papanasam Beach: Cliff-top walk from the Helipad, then the steps down to the beach — strong currents. (Swim only at flagged spots)
11:30 AM — Janardana Swamy Temple: The ancient Vishnu temple above Papanasam. Lunch at the cliff-top cafés after. (Dress code · Hindus only inside)
2:00 PM — Sivagiri Mutt: The ashram and resting place of the reformer Sree Narayana Guru. (Footwear off · quiet)
4:00 PM — Kappil beach & lake: Where the backwater meets the sea: an optional boat ride, then sunset on the sand bar. (Boating paid direct · no swimming)
9:00 PM — Drop-off: Along the coast to Kollam, then NH 66 home to Alappuzha.
Good_To_Know:
🌊 Sea safety: Papanasam has strong currents — swim only between the lifeguard flags; no sea bathing June–September. Kappil's sea is rough: no swimming there at all — boating on the lake only.
🛕 Temple & ashram: Janardana Swamy: modest dress; only Hindus enter the inner temple. Sivagiri: footwear off, shoulders and knees covered, silence near the samadhi.
🧗 On the cliff: The laterite edge crumbles — stay behind railings, no selfies at the edge. Paragliding runs in season with licensed operators only, paid direct.
⏱️ A long day: About 3 hours each way on NH 66, where widening work slows traffic. Prefer a slower pace? Ask us to add a night in Varkala.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver; All Varkala sightseeing drives; Driver bata; No waiting charges

Headline: Sabarimala pilgrimage
Duration: 1 long day · set by your slot
Description: Your own vehicle from Alappuzha to Nilakkal base camp for the 2026-27 Mandala–Makaravilakku season, with an Erumely stop if you wish — the driver waits to bring you home.
Highlights: Virtual Queue slot, Erumely Petta Thullal, Nilakkal base camp, Door to door
Itinerary:
≈4:30 AM — Pickup: From your door — home, hotel, houseboat jetty or Alappuzha station. (Example: 10 AM slot)
On the road — Via Changanassery & Karukachal: About 110 km to Nilakkal through rubber country, with a tea break.
≈6:15 AM — Erumely (optional): Petta Thullal at the Petta Sastha temple and a visit to Vavar Palli. (Tell us when booking)
≈8:30 AM — Nilakkal base camp: Private vehicles stop here; KSRTC chain buses take you on to Pampa. (Bus fare paid direct)
Day — Pampa, the climb & darshan: About 5 km uphill on foot to Sannidhanam, darshan, and the walk back. (Virtual Queue booked by you)
≈11 PM — Home: Your driver waits at Nilakkal and brings you home the same night.
Good_To_Know:
📱 Virtual Queue: Book your darshan slot yourself at sabarimalaonline.org; carry the QR coupon and the same photo ID. Spot-booking counters are limited — don't count on them.
🅿️ Nilakkal & Pampa: Private vehicles are not allowed to Pampa — KSRTC chain buses run from Nilakkal. Save your driver's number and the parking block.
🗓️ Season 2026-27: The temple opens on 16 Nov 2026; Mandala Pooja is on 27 Dec; Makaravilakku in mid-January 2027. Peak days bring police holds and long queues — we re-confirm before you travel.
❤️ The climb: About 5 km of steep forest path — go slow; medical centres with oxygen line the route. Elderly pilgrims and heart patients: check with your doctor first.

Headline: Kumarakom by the lake

7:30 AM — Kumarakom bird sanctuary: A shaded lakeside trail with herons, egrets and cormorants, best in the cool morning. (Entry own expense)
9:30 AM — Vembanad boat & Pathiramanal: Across Kerala's largest lake to a quiet bird island, then a karimeen lunch, own expense. (Boat paid direct)

3:15 PM — Thazhathangady: Old riverside trading street on the Meenachil and its centuries-old Juma Masjid. (Mosque seen from outside)

9:45 AM — Pine forest: Walk under tall pines on the slopes just outside Vagamon town. (Entry own expense)
11:00 AM — Vagamon meadows & lake: Rolling grass hills with the Kurisumala view, then the calm lake. Lunch in town, own expense.

Headline: Illikkal rocks & meadows
Description: Kottayam's wild high country in a day: a forest waterfall at Marmala, the misty rock towers of Illikkal Kallu and the wide green bowl of Ilaveezhapoonchira, 'the valley where no leaves fall'.
Highlights: Illikkal Kallu, Ilaveezhapoonchira, Marmala falls, Misty hill roads
Itinerary:
6:30 AM — Pickup: Kottayam railway station · Kottayam KSRTC bus station · your hotel in town (Breakfast stop at Erattupetta)
8:45 AM — Marmala falls: A tall waterfall in the forest beyond Theekoy, reached by a short estate walk. (View only · no bathing)
10:30 AM — Illikkal Kallu: Three rock peaks at about 3,500 ft, with views to the sea on clear days. Lunch at Melukavu after. (Steep walk · jeep paid direct)

6:45 PM — Drop-off: Kottayam station, KSRTC bus station, or your own stop in town
Good_To_Know:

👟 Fitness: Good for anyone who can manage a steep 20–30 minute climb. Elderly guests can enjoy Ilaveezhapoonchira and the viewpoints near the road.

Headline: Kottayam faith trail
Description: Faith and old Kottayam in a day: two great Shiva temples, St Alphonsa's shrine at Bharananganam, churches with Persian crosses and riverside Thazhathangady.

Day 2 · late morning — Kumari Amman Temple: The ancient shore temple of the virgin goddess. (Men remove shirts · dress code)
Day 2 · ~8:30 PM — Home: About 255 km back to Kottayam — Suchindram temple on the way if it is open.

Headline: Idukki the arch dam trail

Highlights: Idukki Arch Dam, Hill View Park, Kalvari Mount, Nadukani viewpoint

7:00 AM — Pickup: Thodupuzha KSRTC bus station · Muvattupuzha · your hotel on the way (Muvattupuzha 7:00 · Thodupuzha 7:30)
8:45 AM — Nadukani viewpoint: A hilltop pavilion on the climb, looking far down over Moolamattam and the plains. (Photo stop)
10:00 AM — Idukki & Cheruthoni dams: The arch dam between two granite hills; walk the dam top on visitor days. (Visitor days only · tickets online)
11:45 AM — Hill View Park: Gardens and a lookout over the reservoir. Lunch at Cheruthoni after. (Entry own expense)
2:30 PM — Kalvari Mount: A grassy ridge high above the Idukki reservoir and its forested islands — the district's best view. (Short uphill walk)
6:30 PM — Drop-off: Thodupuzha KSRTC bus station, Muvattupuzha, or your own stop on the way

⛰️ Hill roads: About 2 hours up from Thodupuzha on hairpin roads via Moolamattam and Kulamavu. Motion sickness? Sit in front and tell us — we stop at wide spots.

Headline: Waterfalls near Thodupuzha
Description: An easy waterfall day close to home: a forest walk past the stepped cascades of Thommankuthu, the broad curtain of Anayadikuthu and a quiet afternoon by the Malankara reservoir.
Highlights: Thommankuthu Falls, Anayadikuthu Falls, Malankara Dam, Forest walk
Itinerary:
8:00 AM — Pickup: Thodupuzha KSRTC bus station · Muvattupuzha · your hotel on the way (Muvattupuzha 8:00 · Thodupuzha 8:30)
9:15 AM — Thommankuthu Falls: A forest walk up the Kaliyar river past the first of its seven stepped cascades and rock pools. (Forest ticket, paid direct)
11:45 AM — Anayadikuthu Falls: A wide curtain of water just below the road near Thommankuthu town. Lunch in Thodupuzha after, own expense. (Short, steep path)
2:30 PM — Malankara Dam: The calm reservoir at Muttom: lakeside walkway, park and wide water views, with boating when it runs. (Paid direct if any)
5:00 PM — Drop-off: Thodupuzha KSRTC bus station, Muvattupuzha, or your own stop on the way
Good_To_Know:
💧 Water safety: No bathing, swimming or climbing on wet rocks anywhere on this tour — pools look calm but are deep. Children stay within arm's reach at the falls and by the reservoir.
🌧️ Rain & closures: The forest department can close Thommankuthu in heavy rain — we check the evening before. The falls are fullest from June to December; thin in April–May.
🥾 The walk: About 1–2 km of uneven forest path and rock at Thommankuthu, at your own pace. Shoes or sandals with grip; leeches are common in the monsoon.
🚌 Pickup points: Muvattupuzha first, then Thodupuzha — exact times the evening before. Drop-off in the reverse order, or at your own stop on the way.

Headline: Munnar in a day
Description: Kerala's favourite hill station in one long day: roadside waterfalls on the climb, the Tea Museum, rolling estates and the lake at Mattupetty, with Echo Point on the elephant road.
Highlights: Roadside waterfalls, Tea Museum, Mattupetty Dam, Echo Point
Itinerary:
6:00 AM — Pickup: Thodupuzha KSRTC bus station · Muvattupuzha · your hotel on the way (Thodupuzha 6:00 · Muvattupuzha 6:30)
8:15 AM — Cheeyappara & Valara falls: Roadside waterfalls in the Neriamangalam forest. Breakfast at Kothamangalam on the way, own expense. (Fullest in the monsoon)
10:00 AM — Tea Museum, Nullatanni: How tea goes from leaf to cup, with an old rolling machine and a tasting. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
11:15 AM — Tea estate viewpoints: Photo stops among the green estates on the Mattupetty road. (Estates are private land)
11:45 AM — Mattupetty Dam & Echo Point: Lake views and optional boating, then the echo across the water. Lunch in Munnar town after. (Boating paid direct)
7:00 PM — Drop-off: Thodupuzha KSRTC bus station, Muvattupuzha, or your own stop on the way
Good_To_Know:
⏱️ A long day: About 3½ hours each way on the NH 85 ghat via Adimali, with breaks. Eravikulam and Top Station need more time — ask us for a private 2-day trip.
🗓️ Closing days: The Tea Museum is closed on Mondays — that day we stop at a Pallivasal spice garden instead. Boating at Mattupetty depends on the weather and water level.
🐘 Wildlife: Elephants often cross the Mattupetty road — everyone stays inside if we stop. Never feed or approach animals; no flash photos.
🧥 Weather: Cool mornings and misty afternoons — bring a light layer. Heavy-rain alerts can close viewpoints; we check the evening before.

Headline: Vagamon pine & meadows
Description: Kerala's quiet hills, 90 minutes up from Thodupuzha: misty pine forest, rolling green meadows with the Kurisumala skyline, the lake, the adventure park and late views from Thangalpara.

Headline: Munnar & Top Station
Description: Waterfalls on the climb, tea estates to the horizon, the cliff-edge view from Top Station and the Nilgiri tahr of Eravikulam — Munnar is about three hours from Thodupuzha.
Highlights: Waterfalls, Tea gardens, Top Station view, Eravikulam Park
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 7:00 AM — Pickup & drive up: From your door, hotel or the Thodupuzha KSRTC stand; about 88 km via Neriamangalam and Adimali, roughly 3 hours.
Day 1 · 8:00 AM — Cheeyappara & Valara falls: Roadside waterfalls in the Neriamangalam forest — a short photo stop. Breakfast at Adimali. (Fullest in the monsoon)
Day 1 · late morning — Tea Museum: How tea goes from leaf to cup, at Nullatanni. Early lunch in Munnar town. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
Day 1 · afternoon — Mattupetty, Echo Point & Kundala: Lake views and optional boating on the Top Station road. (Boating paid direct)
Day 1 · 3:15 PM — Top Station: A cliff-edge view over the Western Ghats into Tamil Nadu. Overnight in Munnar. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Eravikulam National Park: Park buses take you up Rajamala to see the Nilgiri tahr. (Tickets online · closed ~Feb–Mar)
Day 2 · ~5 PM — Drive home: Leave after lunch; back at your door in Thodupuzha by early evening.

Headline: Thekkady spice & wildlife
Description: Walk a cardamom and pepper plantation, catch a Kathakali or Kalaripayattu show, and take the morning boat into the Periyar Tiger Reserve — under four hours from Thodupuzha.
Highlights: Periyar boat cruise, Spice plantations, Kathakali show, Chellarkovil view
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 7:00 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door, hotel or the Thodupuzha KSRTC stand; about 116 km via Erattupetta and the Kuttikkanam ghat, roughly 4 hours.
Day 1 · afternoon — Spice plantation tour: Cardamom, pepper, cinnamon and coffee with a local guide. (Paid direct)
Day 1 · evening — Kathakali or Kalaripayattu: Kerala's classical dance-drama or martial art at a Kumily theatre. Overnight in Thekkady. (Optional, paid direct)
Day 2 · 7:30 AM — Periyar Lake boat cruise: The first sailing — the best time to see elephants, gaur and deer at the water's edge. (Limited seats · tickets in advance)
Day 2 · late morning — Chellarkovil viewpoint: A cliff-edge view over the Cumbum valley and Tamil Nadu plains.
Day 2 · ~5:30 PM — Drive home: Down the ghat after lunch; back at your door in Thodupuzha by evening.

Headline: Marayoor & Kanthalloor
Description: Kerala's only natural sandalwood forest, Iron Age dolmens, Kanthalloor's fruit farms and the dry forest of Chinnar — the quiet rain-shadow side of Munnar.
Highlights: Sandalwood forest, Muniyara dolmens, Chinnar forest walk, Kanthalloor orchards
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:30 AM — Pickup & drive up: From your door or the Thodupuzha KSRTC stand; about 128 km via Adimali and Munnar, roughly 5 hours.
Day 1 · late morning — Lakkam waterfalls: A forest-department waterfall on the Marayoor road, past Rajamala. (Entry own expense)
Day 1 · afternoon — Sandalwood forest & jaggery: Kerala's only natural sandalwood forest and jaggery in the making. Lunch in town.
Day 1 · 4:00 PM — Muniyara dolmens: Iron Age burial chambers near Kovilkadavu. Overnight in Marayoor or Kanthalloor. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · 7:00 AM — Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary: A guided forest walk in dry thorn forest — look for the grizzled giant squirrel. (Paid direct · booked ahead)
Day 2 · late morning — Kanthalloor farms: Orchards and vegetable terraces; farm stalls sell whatever is in season. (Seasonal)
Day 2 · ~6:30 PM — Drive home: Back past Munnar and down the ghat to your door in Thodupuzha.

🐿️ Chinnar walks: Walks and treks are run by the Forest Department with local guides; numbers are limited, so we book ahead. Dry, hot forest: carry water, a cap and closed shoes.
🍎 Kanthalloor fruit: Apples, plums, oranges and passion fruit ripen in different months — what you see depends on the season. Farms are private: buy at the stalls and ask before entering.
🏨 Your stay: You book your stay in Marayoor or Kanthalloor; homestays and farm resorts are common. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.

Headline: Windy hills of Ramakkalmedu
Description: Idukki's high range in a day: Kalvari Mount, the Anchuruli tunnel lake, spice-town Kattappana and windswept Ramakkalmedu.
Highlights: Kuravan–Kurathi statue, Wind-farm ridge, Anchuruli tunnel lake, Kalvari Mount view
Itinerary:
6:00 AM — Pickup: From your door — home, hotel or Thodupuzha KSRTC stand. Breakfast at Cheruthoni.
8:45 AM — Kalvari Mount: A hilltop view over the blue Idukki reservoir and the Kuravan–Kurathi hills that hold the arch dam. (Entry own expense)
10:15 AM — Anchuruli: Where a long rock-cut tunnel from Irattayar spills into the Idukki lake, ringed by forest. (Tunnel closed · view only)
12:00 PM — Kattappana: Cardamom and pepper country's market town — lunch and spice shopping, own expense.
1:45 PM — Ramakkalmedu: The Kuravan–Kurathi statue, wind turbines and a cliff view over Tamil Nadu. (Entry own expense · very windy)
7:30 PM — Drop-off: Back via Kattappana, Cheruthoni and Kulamavu to your door.

Headline: Kochi a day in the city
Description: Your own vehicle from Thodupuzha to old Kochi: Chinese fishing nets, India's oldest European church, the Dutch Palace murals, Jew Town and a Marine Drive walk.
Highlights: Chinese fishing nets, St Francis Church, Dutch Palace murals, Jew Town
Itinerary:
7:00 AM — Pickup: From your door — home, hotel or Thodupuzha KSRTC stand. Breakfast on the way at Muvattupuzha.
9:15 AM — Fort Kochi: fishing nets & churches: Chinese fishing nets, St Francis Church (Vasco da Gama's first grave) and Santa Cruz Basilica. (Modest dress in the churches)
11:15 AM — Mattancherry Palace: The 'Dutch Palace' with its Ramayana murals and royal portraits. (Closed Fridays · entry own expense)
12:00 PM — Jew Town & Paradesi Synagogue: Antique shops, spice stores and the 1568 synagogue. Lunch here, own expense. (Synagogue closed Fri & Sat)
2:30 PM — Kerala Folklore Museum: Masks, costumes and carved wooden halls from across South India. (Entry own expense)

🚶 Walking: Fort Kochi and Jew Town are best on foot — about 3–4 km of easy walking in all. Wear comfortable shoes; lanes are uneven in places.
🧭 Your day, your way: It's a private trip — add Lulu Mall, a harbour ferry or an early dinner in the city. About 2 hours each way via Muvattupuzha; evening traffic can add 30 minutes.

Headline: Houseboat a night afloat

Headline: Kodaikanal princess of hills

Headline: Thrissur temple town
Description: Kerala's cultural capital in one easy day: Vadakkunnathan on its hill, the two Pooram temples, the Kochi king's palace, India's tallest church and the new Puthur zoo.
Highlights: Vadakkunnathan, India's tallest church, Shakthan palace, Puthur zoo
Itinerary:
8:00 AM — Pickup: Thrissur railway station · Thrissur KSRTC bus station · Swaraj Round
8:30 AM — Vadakkunnathan temple: The great Shiva temple in the Thekkinkadu ground at the heart of the Round — home of Thrissur Pooram. (Hindus only inside · dress code)
9:45 AM — Paramekkavu & Thiruvambady: The two rival temples of the Pooram, a short walk apart. (Dress code)
10:45 AM — Shakthan Thampuran Palace: The Kochi king's Kerala-Dutch palace: bronzes, sculptures, old scripts and a serpent grove. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
12:15 PM — Our Lady of Dolours Basilica: India's tallest church and its Bible Tower. Lunch in town after, own expense. (Modest dress)
2:30 PM — Puthur Zoological Park: Kerala's new open-design zoo in the Puthur hills, with large natural enclosures. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
5:30 PM — Drop-off: Thrissur station, KSRTC bus station, Swaraj Round, or your own stop in the city
Good_To_Know:
🗓️ Closing days: Shakthan Thampuran Palace and Puthur Zoological Park are closed on Mondays. On Mondays we swap in Vilangan Kunnu hill and more time in town — same price.
👗 Temples & church: Vadakkunnathan admits Hindus only. Men: mundu, shirt off inside; women: saree or churidar. Others can walk the Thekkinkadu ground. Modest dress at the Basilica; no phones or bags inside the temples.
🚶 Walking: The temples around the Round are best on foot — about 2–3 km in all. The zoo is large: allow 2 hours and wear comfortable shoes.
🎉 Pooram & festivals: During Thrissur Pooram (April–May) the Round is packed and roads close — we run a shorter plan. Temple timings change on festival days; we confirm the evening before.

Headline: Waterfalls of Athirappilly
Description: Kerala's mightiest waterfalls in a day: the Thumboormuzhi butterfly garden, thundering Athirappilly, roadside Charpa and the forest rapids of Vazhachal on the Chalakudy river.
Highlights: Athirappilly Falls, Vazhachal Falls, Butterfly garden, Charpa Falls
Itinerary:
8:00 AM — Pickup: Thrissur railway station · Thrissur KSRTC bus station · Swaraj Round
9:30 AM — Thumboormuzhi dam & butterfly garden: A riverside garden by the old weir, with a hanging bridge. (Entry own expense)
10:30 AM — Athirappilly Falls: The top viewpoint, then the path to the base if open. Lunch nearby, own expense. (Entry own expense)
1:45 PM — Charpa Falls: A cascade right beside the forest road. (Flows in the monsoon)
2:00 PM — Vazhachal Falls: Wide rapids over black rock at the forest's edge. (Viewing area only)
5:30 PM — Drop-off: Thrissur station, KSRTC bus station, Swaraj Round, or your own stop in the city
Good_To_Know:
🌧️ Rain & closures: The forest department closes the falls, or the path to the base, in heavy rain or high water. If a stop is shut, we spend longer at the others — we check the evening before.
🚯 Plastic-free forest: Disposable plastic is not allowed in the forest area; bags may be checked at the entry. Bring a reusable bottle; snacks in boxes, not plastic covers.
🐒 Monkeys & wildlife: Monkeys at the falls snatch food and bags — keep snacks out of sight. Elephants sometimes cross the forest road; everyone stays inside if we stop.
🥾 The walk down: The path to the base of Athirappilly is steep, with many uneven steps — the climb back is slow. Wear shoes with grip; skip it if you have knee or heart trouble.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Falls and garden entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)

Headline: Guruvayur temple & beach
Description: An early start for darshan at Guruvayur's Sri Krishna temple and Mammiyoor, the Punnathur Kotta elephants, the ancient Palayur church and an afternoon on Chavakkad beach.
Highlights: Guruvayur temple, Punnathur Kotta, Palayur church, Chavakkad beach
Itinerary:
6:00 AM — Pickup: Thrissur railway station · Thrissur KSRTC bus station · Swaraj Round
6:45 AM — Guruvayur Sri Krishna temple: Darshan at 'the Dwarka of the South'; phones and bags to the counters. (Hindus only · strict dress code)
10:45 AM — Mammiyoor temple & lunch: The Shiva temple next door, then lunch, own expense. (Dress code)
12:45 PM — Punnathur Kotta: The temple's elephant yard in an old palace compound. (Entry own expense)
2:15 PM — Palayur church: One of India's oldest churches, believed founded by St Thomas the Apostle. (Modest dress)
3:15 PM — Chavakkad beach: A wide, quiet beach with fishing boats — sea breeze before the drive home. (Walk only · no swimming)
5:30 PM — Drop-off: Thrissur station, KSRTC bus station, Swaraj Round, or your own stop in the city
Good_To_Know:
👗 Dress code: Men: mundu, no shirt (a shawl is fine). Women: saree, churidar or long skirt. No jeans, shorts or T-shirts. Mundus and sarees are sold near the temple if needed.
📵 At the temple: Phones, cameras, bags and footwear are not allowed inside — use the paid counters. Queues of 2–4 hours on weekends, Ekadasi and wedding days; keep water and medicines handy.
🙏 Non-Hindu guests: The two temples admit Hindus only. You can see the East Nada from outside, walk the temple town and join us at the elephant yard. Palayur church and the beach are open to everyone.
🌊 Beach & elephants: Chavakkad beach is for walking only — strong currents, no swimming. At Punnathur Kotta stay behind the barriers; no feeding or touching the elephants.

Headline: Muziris the ancient port
Description: Two thousand years of Kerala's spice port in a day: Kodungallur's ancient temple, India's oldest mosque, St Thomas's landing place, a Portuguese fort and the Paliam palace.
Highlights: India's oldest mosque, Kodungallur temple, Portuguese fort, Paliam palace
Itinerary:
8:00 AM — Pickup: Thrissur railway station · Thrissur KSRTC bus station · Swaraj Round
9:15 AM — Kodungallur Bhagavathy temple: The ancient Kurumba Bhagavathy temple of the Bharani festival. (Hindus only inside · dress code)
10:15 AM — Cheraman Juma Masjid: Believed to be India's oldest mosque, restored in old Kerala style. (Modest dress · head cover for women)
11:30 AM — Azhikode Marthoma shrine: Where St Thomas is believed to have landed in AD 52. Lunch nearby, own expense. (Modest dress)
1:45 PM — Kottappuram fort: Ruins of the 1523 Portuguese fort on the Periyar bank. (Open ruins · uneven ground)
2:45 PM — Paliam palace & Nalukettu: Home of Kochi's hereditary prime ministers, now two museums. (Check timings · entry own expense)
5:45 PM — Drop-off: Thrissur station, KSRTC bus station, Swaraj Round, or your own stop in the city
Good_To_Know:
🗓️ Timings & days: The Paliam museums open about 10 AM–5 PM; Muziris sites can close on some weekdays — we check the evening before. During Kodungallur Bharani (March–April) the town is packed and we change the plan.
👗 What to wear: Shoulders and knees covered everywhere; women cover their heads at the mosque. The Kodungallur temple admits Hindus only inside — others wait at the gate area.
🚶 Walking: Short walks at each stop; Kottappuram fort is an open site with uneven ground. The palaces are old buildings with steps and low doorways — take it slowly.
🌍 Many faiths, one coast: Temple, mosque and church in one morning — please be quiet at prayer times. Friday midday prayers: we visit the mosque earlier or later that day.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Museum entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Clothes covering shoulders and knees; Scarf or shawl; Hat and water bottle; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Kathakali school by the Nila
Description: A morning inside Kerala Kalamandalam, watching Kathakali and Mohiniyattam classes in session, lunch by the river Nila at Cheruthuruthy, and a lakeside evening at Vazhani dam.
Highlights: Kathakali classes, Koothambalam theatre, River Nila, Vazhani dam
Itinerary:
7:45 AM — Pickup: Thrissur railway station · Thrissur KSRTC bus station · Swaraj Round
9:30 AM — Kerala Kalamandalam guided tour: Live classes in the kalaris, the carved Koothambalam theatre, the art gallery and the poet Vallathol's old campus on the river. (Working days only · entry own expense)
1:15 PM — Lunch at Cheruthuruthy: Kerala lunch in the village, own expense.
2:15 PM — Bharathapuzha riverside: A short walk on the banks of the Nila, Kerala's river of poets. (Water level permitting)
3:15 PM — Vazhani dam & garden: Gardens, a hanging bridge and the reservoir below the Machad hills. (Entry own expense)
6:00 PM — Drop-off: Thrissur station, KSRTC bus station, Swaraj Round, or your own stop in the city
Good_To_Know:
🗓️ Tour days: Kalamandalam tours run 9:30 AM–1 PM on working days only — no Sundays or holidays. Closed April–May and for about 10 days each at Onam and Christmas; we book your place ahead.
👣 In the kalaris: Footwear comes off in the classrooms — wear sandals that slip on and off easily. Watch quietly; ask before photographing students.
🌊 By the river: The Nila is shallow most of the year but has sudden deep pools and soft sand. Walking only on the riverbank — no wading or bathing.
🎟️ Entry fees: Kalamandalam and Vazhani dam tickets are paid direct at the gate. Some classes may be off on a given day; the tour still covers the campus and gallery.

Headline: Valparai via Malakkappara
Description: Past Athirappilly falls and through 55 km of rainforest to the Tamil Nadu border at Malakkappara, a night in Valparai's tea hills, then down the 40 hairpins to Aliyar.
Highlights: Malakkappara forest, Valparai tea hills, Lion-tailed macaques, 40 hairpins
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door, hotel, Thrissur station or bus stand; breakfast at Chalakudy.
Day 1 · 8:15 AM — Athirappilly & the forest road: A viewpoint stop at Athirappilly Falls, then through the Vazhachal and Sholayar forests to Malakkappara. (Road open 6 AM–6 PM only)
Day 1 · afternoon — Valparai & Nallamudi viewpoint: Lunch and check-in, then a walk through tea to the Nallamudi cliff-top view. Overnight in Valparai. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · 8:00 AM — Puthuthottam rainforest: Rainforest where lion-tailed macaques are often seen by the road. (Watch from the vehicle side)
Day 2 · morning — 40 hairpins to Aliyar: Loam's viewpoint on the way down, then the Aliyar dam and park. (Monkey Falls if open)
Day 2 · ~6:00 PM — Drive home: Lunch at Pollachi, then via Palakkad to your door in Thrissur.
Good_To_Know:
🌳 Forest road: The Athirappilly–Malakkappara road is open to vehicles only from 6 AM to 6 PM, with check posts at both ends. No getting out inside the forest; elephants use this road and stops are monitored.
🪪 Tamil Nadu entry: Interstate permit and border tax are billed at actual cost. Tamil Nadu has ordered an e-pass for Valparai — we apply if needed and re-check before you go.
🌀 Down via Aliyar: Day 2 descends the Aliyar ghat — about 40 hairpin bends, taken slowly with brake-cooling stops. Carry motion sickness tablets if bends bother you.
🚯 No plastic: Disposable plastic is banned on the forest roads and in Valparai; bags may be checked. Bring a refillable bottle; keep snacks in boxes.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; Athirappilly–Valparai sightseeing; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry fees and any e-pass charge; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Photo ID; Light jacket; Motion sickness tablets; Refillable water bottle

Headline: Munnar tea hills
Description: Waterfalls on the climb, tea estates as far as you can see and the Nilgiri tahr of Eravikulam — Kerala's favourite hill station, about five hours from Thrissur.
Highlights: Waterfalls, Tea gardens, Mattupetty Dam, Eravikulam Park
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive up: From your door, hotel, Thrissur station, the bus stand or Cochin Airport; about 160 km via Angamaly, Perumbavoor and Kothamangalam, roughly 5 hours.
Day 1 · 9:30 AM — Cheeyappara & Valara falls: Roadside waterfalls in the Neriamangalam forest — a short photo stop. (Fullest in the monsoon)
Day 1 · midday — Tea Museum: How tea goes from leaf to cup, at Nullatanni. Lunch in Munnar town. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
Day 1 · afternoon — Mattupetty Dam & Echo Point: Lake views and optional boating on the Top Station road. Overnight in Munnar. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · morning — Eravikulam National Park: Park buses take you up Rajamala to see the Nilgiri tahr. (Tickets online · closed ~Feb–Mar)
Day 2 · ~6:30 PM — Drive home: Leave after lunch; back at your door in Thrissur by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🐐 Eravikulam: Tickets are sold online in time slots — book a few days ahead; we can help. Closed for the tahr calving season, usually February–March; then we go to Top Station instead.
🍃 Tea & spices: Tea estates are private land — photograph from the roadside. Spice gardens at Pallivasal and Kallar are optional, paid direct.
🏨 Your stay: You book your hotel; Munnar town, Pothamedu and Chithirapuram are popular. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
🧥 Weather & roads: Cool mornings, cold in December–January — bring a layer. In heavy-rain alerts hill roads can close at night — we plan to be off the ghat before dark.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; All Munnar sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Park, museum and boating fees; Tolls and parking

Headline: Hilltops of Nelliyampathy
Description: Your own vehicle for a cool day in the hills: Pothundy dam, ten hairpins through the forest, then orange farms, tea estates and cliff-top views at Seethargundu — two hours from Thrissur.
Highlights: 10 hairpin bends, Seethargundu view, Orange farm, Pothundy dam
Itinerary:
6:30 AM — Pickup: From your door, hotel, Thrissur station or the bus stand; via the Kuthiran tunnel and Vadakkanchery, breakfast on the way.
8:45 AM — Pothundy dam: A quick stop at the old earth dam at the foot of the hills, by the forest check post. (Photos only)
9:15 AM — Up the ten hairpins: A 17 km forest climb to Kaikatty, with stops at safe viewpoints. (Forest check post on the way)
10:15 AM — Seethargundu viewpoint: Cliff-top views over the Kollengode plains and a seasonal waterfall. (Short walk)
11:45 AM — Orange farm & Kesavanpara: The government orange farm, tea and cardamom estates and the Kesavanpara rock view. Lunch in the hills, own expense.
6:30 PM — Drop-off: Down the ghat by mid-afternoon; back to your door in Thrissur.
Good_To_Know:
🛣️ Hairpin road: About 10 hairpins between Pothundy and Kaikatty — carry motion sickness tablets if needed. Vehicles are logged at the forest check post; we go up early and come down before dark.
🌧️ Weather: Best from September to February; cool and misty most mornings. Heavy monsoon rain can bring landslips on the ghat — we re-check the day before.
🍽️ Food & cash: Few places to eat in the hills — we stop for a proper breakfast on the way up. No ATM or fuel up there: carry cash for entry and shops.
🐘 Wildlife: Elephants and gaur sometimes cross near the estates at dawn and dusk. Stay in the vehicle if animals are on the road; your driver will wait.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver; All Nelliyampathy sightseeing drives; Driver bata; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Meals; Entry, jeep safari and farm shop; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Light jacket; Walking shoes; Motion sickness tablets; Cash (no ATM up the hill)

Headline: Wayanad caves & forests
Description: Up the nine hairpins of the Thamarassery ghat to Kerala's green north: forest lakes, the country's largest earth dam and Edakkal's ancient carvings — your own vehicle and driver.
Highlights: Edakkal Caves, Banasura Dam, Pookode Lake, Thamarassery ghat
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive to Wayanad: From your door in Thrissur — about 190 km via Kunnamkulam, Kuttippuram, Kozhikode and the Thamarassery ghat, roughly 6 hours with breaks. (Stay booked by you)
Day 1 · midday — Lakkidi viewpoint & Pookode Lake: The view back down the ghat, then a forest lake right on the way in. (Boating optional, paid direct)
Day 2 · morning — Edakkal Caves: A short, steep climb to caves with prehistoric rock carvings. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)
Day 2 · afternoon — Banasura Sagar Dam: India's largest earth dam, with green islands in the reservoir. (Entry & boating own expense)
Day 2 · or swap in — Chembra, Soochipara or Kuruva: A peak trek, a forest waterfall or bamboo-raft river islands — pick one. (Seasonal · we check if open)
Day 3 — Drive home: Leave after breakfast; back at your door in Thrissur by mid-afternoon.
Good_To_Know:
🪨 Edakkal Caves: Closed on Mondays — we plan around it. The climb is steep: not ideal for elders or small children.
🌧️ Seasonal spots: Kuruva Island closes in the monsoon and has a daily visitor cap; treks and falls can shut after heavy rain. We check on the day and swap stops.
🏨 Your stay: You book your resort or homestay; Kalpetta and Vythiri are central. Your driver's night allowance is in our price.
⛰️ The ghat: Thamarassery ghat jams on weekends and holidays. We start early both ways to beat the queues.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 3 days; All Wayanad sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowances; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry, boating and trek fees; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Trekking shoes; Raincoat; Light jacket; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Ooty queen of hills
Description: The Nilgiris' classic hill stations: gardens, a lake and the highest peak in Ooty, tea country in Coonoor, and the famous toy train — your vehicle, your pace.
Highlights: Botanical Garden, Doddabetta Peak, Coonoor tea, Toy train (opt.)
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:30 AM — Pickup & drive to Ooty: From your door in Thrissur — about 210 km via Palakkad, Coimbatore, Mettupalayam and the Coonoor ghat, roughly 6–7 hours. (Stay booked by you)
Day 1 · evening — Ooty Lake: An easy first evening: a walk or a boat on the lake. (Boating optional, paid direct)

Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry, boating and toy train tickets; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals

Headline: Kodaikanal princess of hills

Highlights: Kodai Lake, Coaker's Walk, Pillar Rocks, Pine forest

Headline: Malampuzha & Palakkad Fort

9:30 AM — Palakkad Fort: Tipu Sultan's 18th-century fort with its moat, ramparts and a small Hanuman temple inside. (Free to walk the grounds)

🐘 Wildlife: Elephants and gaur sometimes cross near the estates at dawn and dusk. Everyone stays inside if animals are on the road; we wait.
