Exclusions: Breakfast and lunch; Entry fees, jeep safari and farm shop; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Light jacket; Walking shoes; Motion sickness tablets; Cash (no ATM up the hill)

Headline: Kollengode village trail
Description: Green paddy fields, toddy palms and the blue wall of the Nelliyampathy hills: Kollengode's old palace and lanes, two quiet dams at Chulliyar and Meenkara, and the Muthalamada mango belt.
Highlights: Paddy fields & palms, Kollengode palace, Chulliyar dam, Mango orchards
Itinerary:
8:00 AM — Pickup: Palakkad Junction (Olavakkode) · Palakkad KSRTC bus station · your hotel in town
9:00 AM — Kollengode palace & lanes: The old palace of the Vengunad royal family, seen from outside, and the village lanes around it. (Outside view only)
9:45 AM — Paddy-field drive: Slow roads through fields and palms under the hills, with photo stops. (Greenest Jul–Oct)
10:30 AM — Chulliyar dam: A quiet reservoir under the hills — a walk on the bund and wide views. (Photos from the bund)
11:45 AM — Meenkara dam & Muthalamada: Meenkara's small garden, then the mango orchards of Muthalamada. Lunch in Kollengode, own expense. (Mangoes Feb–May)
4:00 PM — Drop-off: Palakkad Junction, KSRTC bus station, or your own stop in town
Good_To_Know:
🌾 Best season: Fields are greenest from July to October and again after the second crop is planted. Mango season in Muthalamada is roughly February to May.
📸 Photos & manners: The fields are private farms — walk only on the bunds and ask before photographing people. The palace is a private home: photos from the road only.
☀️ Heat: Midday is hot and shade is scarce at the dams. Hat, sunscreen and water make the day easier.
💧 At the dams: No swimming or climbing on the spillway at Chulliyar or Meenkara. Garden hours and access can change — we check the week before.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Garden entry and fruit you buy; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Hat and sunscreen; Comfortable shoes; Water bottle; Cash for small shops

Headline: Dhoni falls & forest
Description: A guided forest walk to Dhoni falls in the cool of the morning, then lunch on the way and an easy afternoon in the Kanjirapuzha dam gardens near Mannarkkad.
Highlights: Guided forest trek, Dhoni falls, Kanjirapuzha gardens, Reserve forest
Itinerary:
7:00 AM — Pickup: Palakkad Junction (Olavakkode) · Palakkad KSRTC bus station · your hotel in town
7:45 AM — Dhoni forest trek: A guided walk of a few kilometres through the reserve forest with the forest department. (Guide fee own expense)
9:30 AM — Dhoni falls: Rest by the cascade in the forest, then the walk back down. (No bathing)
12:30 PM — Lunch on the way: Lunch at Kalladikode or Mannarkkad on the Kozhikode road, own expense.
2:00 PM — Kanjirapuzha dam & gardens: Gardens and lawns below the dam, with views of the Western Ghats. (Entry own expense)
5:30 PM — Drop-off: Palakkad Junction, KSRTC bus station, or your own stop in town
Good_To_Know:
🥾 The trek: Uneven forest path with some steep, rocky parts — about 3 hours there and back. Not for guests with knee or heart trouble; children with an adult only.
🌳 Forest rules: Treks run only with a forest department guide; group size and timings are set by them. The forest may close in heavy rain or when elephants are about — we confirm the day before.
🩸 Leeches & rain: Leeches are common in the monsoon; socks and salt help. Wet rocks near the falls are slippery — no bathing, no climbing.
🚯 Plastic-free: No disposable plastic inside the forest; bags may be checked. Bring a reusable bottle; we refill water in the vehicle.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Trek fee, guide and garden entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Shoes with good grip; Socks and a raincoat; Reusable water bottle; Cash for trek and entry

Headline: Coimbatore airport transfer
Description: Coimbatore is Palakkad's nearest airport. We pick you up at your door anywhere in Palakkad, cross the Walayar border with the papers ready and drop you at departures — or meet you at arrivals.
Highlights: Doorstep pickup, Walayar border sorted, Departures drop-off, Arrivals pickup too
Itinerary:
Pickup — Your door: Home or hotel in Palakkad town, Olavakkode, Kanjikode, Chittur or nearby — at the time we agree for your flight.
On the road — ~65 km via Walayar: About 1.5–2 hours on NH 544 through Kanjikode and the Walayar border into Tamil Nadu, then across Coimbatore. (Interstate permit arranged by us)
Drop-off — Coimbatore International Airport: Departures kerb at Peelamedu, off Avinashi Road. Reverse trips start from the arrivals exit. (No waiting charges on arrivals)
Good_To_Know:
✈️ Timing your trip: Leave about 4 hours before an international flight and 3 hours before a domestic one. Coimbatore city traffic is heavy from 8 to 10 AM and 5 to 8 PM — we plan around it.
🛂 Border crossing: The trip enters Tamil Nadu at Walayar; the interstate permit and border tax are billed at actual cost. Keep a photo ID handy in case of a check at the border.
🧳 Luggage: Hatchbacks and sedans suit 2–3 people with check-in bags. Families with large bags: choose an MPV, Premium SUV or Traveller.
🔁 Landing in Coimbatore?: Share your flight number; we track delays and meet you at the arrivals exit with a name board. We track your flight — no waiting charges if it lands late.
Inclusions: Door-to-door pickup; No waiting charges on arrivals; Driver bata; Fuel and per-km charges
Exclusions: Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Passport / ID and tickets; Flight number shared with us; Photo ID for the border; Water for the drive

Headline: Cochin airport transfer
Description: Flying out of Cochin International? We pick you up at your door anywhere in Palakkad and drive you down NH 544 to the right terminal — or meet you at arrivals and bring you home.
Highlights: Doorstep pickup, ~120 km, about 3 hrs, T1 / T3 drop-off, Arrivals pickup too
Itinerary:
Pickup — Your door: Home or hotel in Palakkad town, Olavakkode, Kuzhalmannam, Alathur or nearby — at the time we agree for your flight.
On the road — ~120 km on NH 544: About 3 hours via Alathur, Vadakkanchery, the Kuthiran tunnels, Thrissur bypass, Chalakudy and Angamaly — longer at peak hours. (Tea break on the way)
Drop-off — Cochin International Airport: Domestic (T1) or international (T3) departures. Reverse trips start from the arrivals exit. (No waiting charges on arrivals)
Good_To_Know:
✈️ Timing your trip: Leave about 5.5 hours before an international flight and 4.5 hours before a domestic one. Thrissur, Chalakudy and Angamaly jam at peak hours — we plan around them.
🛫 Which terminal?: Domestic flights use T1; international flights use T3. Check your ticket and tell us — we drop you at the right kerb.
🧳 Luggage: Hatchbacks and sedans suit 2–3 people with check-in bags. Families with large bags: choose an MPV, Premium SUV or Traveller.
🔁 Landing in Kochi?: Share your flight number; we track delays and meet you at the arrivals exit with a name board. We track your flight — no waiting charges if it lands late.
Inclusions: Door-to-door pickup; No waiting charges on arrivals; Driver bata; Fuel and per-km charges
Exclusions: Tolls and airport parking
What_To_Carry: Passport / ID and tickets; Flight number shared with us; Terminal (T1 / T3) noted; Water for the drive

Headline: Silent Valley rainforest
Description: Kerala's last untouched rainforest: up the Attappadi ghat to Mukkali, then the forest department's own vehicle deep into Silent Valley to the Sairandhri watchtower and the Kunthipuzha river.
Highlights: Untouched rainforest, Sairandhri watchtower, Lion-tailed macaques, Attappadi ghat
Itinerary:
6:30 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door, hotel, Palakkad Junction or the KSRTC stand; breakfast at Mannarkkad on the way.
8:00 AM — Up the Attappadi ghat: Past the Anamooli forest check post and up the hairpins to Mukkali on the Bhavani river. (Motion sickness? Tell us)
8:45 AM — Mukkali reception: Report to the forest-department reception with your booking and photo ID. Our vehicle parks here. (Booked with Kerala Forest Dept)
9:00 AM — Into Silent Valley: About 23 km by forest-department vehicle to Sairandhri: the watchtower over the valley and, as the guide allows, a walk down to the Kunthipuzha river. (Forest trip paid direct)
1:30 PM — Lunch at Mukkali: A simple Kerala lunch near the reception, own expense, and a last look at the Bhavani river.
5:30 PM — Drop-off: Down the ghat by mid-afternoon, tea at Mannarkkad, then back to your door in Palakkad.
Good_To_Know:
🎫 Book well ahead: Silent Valley is entered only in forest-department vehicles from Mukkali, with limited seats each day. Book with the Kerala Forest Department before you confirm with us — we can help, and we re-confirm the slot.
🛣️ Attappadi ghat: A hairpin climb from Anamooli up to Mukkali — carry motion sickness tablets if bends bother you. We leave early to reach Mukkali before your forest trip starts.
🚯 Forest rules: No plastic, no music, no feeding animals; stay with the guide on every walk. Little or no mobile signal beyond Mukkali.
🌧️ Season & leeches: The forest department may cut short or cancel trips in heavy rain; we re-check the day before. Leeches in the wet months — wear socks and closed shoes.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver; Palakkad–Mukkali drive both ways; Driver bata; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Meals; Forest-department trip, entry and camera fees; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Photo ID and forest booking; Closed shoes and socks; Light rain jacket; Refillable water bottle

Headline: Jungle of Parambikulam
Description: A night inside one of Kerala's best-kept tiger reserves: through Pollachi and the Topslip forest to Parambikulam, with jungle safari, giant teak and bamboo rafting on your reserve package.
Highlights: Tiger reserve stay, Jungle safari, Kannimara teak, Bamboo rafting
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door, hotel, Palakkad Junction or the KSRTC stand; across the border at Gopalapuram, breakfast in Pollachi.
Day 1 · 8:45 AM — Anamalai forest & Topslip: Through the Sethumadai check post and up the forest road to Topslip on the Tamil Nadu side. (Forest fees paid at the gate)
Day 1 · 10:30 AM — Parambikulam check-in: Report at the tiger reserve reception and check in to your stay inside the reserve. (Stay & package booked by you)
Day 1 · afternoon — Jungle safari: The reserve's own safari through teak and grassland — gaur, deer, elephants and, with luck, a tiger. Kannimara teak on the way. (Reserve vehicle · paid direct)
Day 2 · morning — Rafting or nature walk: A guided activity from your package — bamboo rafting on the reservoir or a forest trek with a tribal guide. (As per your PTR package)
Day 2 · ~5:30 PM — Drive home: Check-out, back through Topslip, lunch in Pollachi, then to your door in Palakkad.
Good_To_Know:
🎫 Book with PTR first: Stays, safaris and rafting inside Parambikulam are run by the tiger reserve and need booking well ahead. Book your package first; we plan the drive around your check-in and activity times.
🛂 Via Tamil Nadu: The road in runs through Pollachi and Topslip in Tamil Nadu; permit and border tax are billed at actual cost. Forest check posts log every vehicle and close in the evening — we arrive early.
🐘 Inside the reserve: Sightseeing is in reserve vehicles with guides; our vehicle takes you to your stay and waits. No plastic, no music, no getting out on the forest road; mobile signal is weak.
🌧️ Season: Heavy monsoon rain can stop activities or close the reserve for a few days; we re-check before you go. Leeches in the wet months — socks and closed shoes help.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; Palakkad–Parambikulam drive both ways; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your stay and PTR package; Meals; Forest entry, safari and vehicle fees; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Photo ID and PTR booking; Closed shoes and socks; Light jacket; Refillable water bottle

Headline: Valparai 40 hairpins up
Description: Across the border to Pollachi and Aliyar dam, up 40 numbered hairpins to Valparai's tea estates and rainforest, a cool night in the hills — and home the next evening.
Highlights: 40 hairpins, Valparai tea hills, Lion-tailed macaques, Aliyar dam
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:30 AM — Pickup & drive: From your door, hotel, Palakkad Junction or the KSRTC stand; breakfast at Pollachi.
Day 1 · 9:00 AM — Aliyar dam: A short stop at the reservoir and park at the foot of the hills. (Monkey Falls only if open)
Day 1 · 9:45 AM — 40 hairpins to Valparai: The famous climb, with a stop at Loam's viewpoint over the Aliyar lake. (Slow, with cooling stops)
Day 1 · afternoon — Valparai & Nallamudi viewpoint: Lunch and check-in, then a walk through tea to the Nallamudi cliff-top view. Overnight in Valparai. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · 8:00 AM — Puthuthottam rainforest: Rainforest where lion-tailed macaques are often seen by the road. (Watch from the vehicle side)
Day 2 · ~5:00 PM — Down & drive home: Down the hairpins after check-out, lunch at Pollachi, back at your door in Palakkad.
Good_To_Know:
🪪 Tamil Nadu entry: Valparai is in Tamil Nadu: interstate permit and border tax are billed at actual cost. An e-pass for Valparai has been ordered — we apply if it is needed and re-check before you go.
🌀 The hairpins: About 40 numbered hairpin bends between Aliyar and Valparai, taken slowly both ways. Carry motion sickness tablets if bends bother you.
🌧️ Weather: Cool and misty most of the year; heavy rain from June to August. Waterfalls and viewpoints can close in heavy rain — we reorder stops.
🚯 No plastic: Disposable plastic is restricted in Valparai and the forest; bags may be checked. Bring a refillable bottle; keep snacks in boxes.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; Aliyar and Valparai sightseeing; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry fees and any e-pass charge; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Photo ID; Light jacket; Motion sickness tablets; Refillable water bottle

Headline: Ooty queen of hills
Description: The Nilgiris in two easy days from Palakkad: tea country in Coonoor, Ooty's gardens and lake, the highest peak at Doddabetta and Dolphin's Nose on the way home.
Highlights: Botanical Garden, Doddabetta Peak, Coonoor tea, Dolphin's Nose
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive to Ooty: From your door in Palakkad — about 150 km via Walayar, Coimbatore, Mettupalayam and the Coonoor ghat, roughly 5 hours with breaks.
Day 1 · 10:30 AM — Coonoor — Sim's Park: Tea country and a hillside garden on the way up. (Entry own expense)
Day 1 · afternoon — Botanical Garden & Ooty Lake: Lunch and check-in, then Ooty's 1840s gardens and a walk or boat on the lake. (Stay booked by you)
Day 2 · 8:00 AM — Doddabetta Peak: The highest point in the Nilgiris, best before the clouds roll in. (Entry own expense)
Day 2 · late morning — Dolphin's Nose, Coonoor: A famous valley lookout on the way down. (Stay behind the railings)
Day 2 · ~6:00 PM — Drive home: Down the ghat, lunch near Mettupalayam, back at your door in Palakkad.
Good_To_Know:
🎫 Nilgiris e-pass: Every vehicle entering the Nilgiris needs a Tamil Nadu e-pass — we apply for it. Single-use plastic is banned: carry refillable steel bottles.
🪪 Tamil Nadu entry: Ooty is in Tamil Nadu: interstate permit, border tax and green fee are billed at actual cost. We re-check entry rules before you travel.
🚂 Toy train: Want the Nilgiri Mountain Railway? Book on IRCTC early; we meet you at the other station. Seats sell out and timings change.
🧥 Weather: Cold nights all year — bring warm clothes. The ghat has many hairpins; carry motion sickness tablets.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 2 days; Ooty and Coonoor sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowance; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry, boating and toy train tickets; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Warm jacket; Photo ID; Refillable water bottle; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Kodaikanal princess of hills
Description: A star-shaped lake, cliff-edge walks and pillar rocks in the Palani hills, with the Palani hill temple on the way home — your own vehicle and driver from Palakkad.
Highlights: Kodai Lake, Coaker's Walk, Pillar Rocks, Palani temple
Itinerary:
Day 1 · 6:00 AM — Pickup & drive to Kodaikanal: From your door in Palakkad — about 175 km via Pollachi, Udumalpet, Palani and the Kodai ghat, roughly 6 hours. (Stay booked by you)
Day 1 · evening — Kodai Lake: A walk, a cycle or a boat round the star-shaped lake. (Boating paid direct)
Day 2 · morning — Coaker's Walk & Bryant Park: A cliff-edge path with views to the plains, then the gardens. (Entry own expense)
Day 2 · afternoon — Pillar Rocks, pine forest & Guna Caves viewpoint: Granite pillars, tall pines and the famous caves lookout. (Entry own expense)
Day 3 · late morning — Palani hill temple (optional): Darshan at the Murugan temple on the way down — by winch, rope car or steps. (Allow 2–3 hrs)
Day 3 · ~6:30 PM — Drive home: Lunch at Palani or Pollachi; back at your door in Palakkad by evening.
Good_To_Know:
🎫 Kodaikanal e-pass: Tourist vehicles need a Tamil Nadu e-pass for Kodaikanal — we apply for it. Plastic is restricted: carry refillable bottles.
🪪 Tamil Nadu entry: Interstate permit, border tax and green fee are billed at actual cost. We re-check entry rules before you travel.
🌫️ Viewpoints: Mist can hide Pillar Rocks and Coaker's Walk — mornings are usually clearer. We reorder stops for the best views.
🛕 Palani temple: Queues are long on festival days and weekends — tell us if you'd rather skip it. Footwear is left below; dress modestly.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver for 3 days; Kodaikanal sightseeing drives; Driver bata and night allowances; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Your hotel; Meals; Entry, boating and temple fees; Permits, border tax, tolls, parking — at actuals
What_To_Carry: Warm jacket; Photo ID; Walking shoes; Cash for entry fees

Headline: Guruvayur temple day
Description: Your own vehicle for early darshan at Guruvayur's Sri Krishna temple and Mammiyoor, the Punnathur Kotta elephants and Palayur church — home by evening.
Highlights: Guruvayur temple, Punnathur Kotta, Mammiyoor temple, Palayur church
Itinerary:
5:00 AM — Pickup: From your door, hotel, Palakkad Jn or KSRTC stand; about 2 hours via Thrissur. (Early start)
7:15 AM — Guruvayur Sri Krishna temple: Darshan at 'the Dwarka of the South'; phones, bags and footwear to the counters. Breakfast after. (Hindus only · strict dress code)
10:45 AM — Mammiyoor temple & lunch: The Shiva temple next door, then a temple-town lunch, own expense. (Dress code)
12:45 PM — Punnathur Kotta: The temple's elephant yard in an old palace compound. (Entry own expense)
2:00 PM — Palayur church: One of India's oldest churches, believed founded by St Thomas the Apostle. (Optional · modest dress)
6:00 PM — Drop-off: Back via Thrissur to your door in Palakkad.
Good_To_Know:
👗 Dress code: Men: mundu, no shirt (a shawl is fine). Women: saree, churidar or long skirt. No jeans, shorts or T-shirts. Mundus and sarees are sold near the temple if needed.
📵 At the temple: Phones, cameras, bags and footwear are not allowed inside — use the paid counters. Queues of 2–4 hours on weekends, Ekadasi and wedding days; keep water and medicines handy.
🙏 Non-Hindu guests: The temples admit Hindus only. You can see the East Nada from outside, walk the temple town and visit the elephant yard. Palayur church is open to everyone.
🚐 Your day, your pace: Want an earlier start or more time in the queue? Just tell us. Add Chavakkad beach or Thrissur's Vadakkunnathan in the evening — ask for a quote.
Inclusions: Private vehicle and driver; Temple-to-temple drives in Guruvayur; Driver bata; No waiting charges
Exclusions: Meals; Offerings, special darshan & elephant-yard entry; Tolls and parking
What_To_Carry: Mundu / saree / churidar; Small pouch for medicines; Water bottle; Cash for counters

Headline: Nilambur teak country
Description: Cross a hanging bridge to the world's oldest teak plantation, then the Teak Museum, Adyanpara falls and the forest at Nedumkayam.
Highlights: Oldest teak plantation, Hanging bridge, Teak Museum, Adyanpara falls
Itinerary:
7:00 AM — Pickup: Malappuram KSRTC bus station · Tirur railway station · Calicut Airport (on request) (Tirur 7:00 · Malappuram 7:45)
9:15 AM — Conolly's Plot: 1840s teak on the Chaliyar bank, over a hanging footbridge. (Entry own expense)
11:00 AM — Teak Museum, Nilambur: Teak history, a giant root and a garden trail. Lunch in Nilambur after, own expense. (Check closing day)
1:45 PM — Adyanpara falls: A wide cascade over rocks near Kurumbalangode. (Closed in heavy rain)
3:45 PM — Nedumkayam forest: Forest on the Karimpuzha, an old wooden bridge and Dawson's grave. (Forest rules apply)
7:15 PM — Drop-off: Malappuram, Tirur station, Calicut Airport, or your own stop on the way
Good_To_Know:
🗓️ Opening days: The Teak Museum keeps a weekly closing day and Conolly's Plot follows forest timings — we confirm both before your date. Waterfalls and the forest stop can close at short notice after heavy rain.
🌉 Hanging bridge: The footbridge sways and takes a limited number of people at a time — the staff count you across. Hold the rails; not ideal for anyone with a fear of heights.
💧 At the falls: Rocks are slippery all year and the pools are deep — viewing only, no bathing. Leeches in the monsoon months on the forest paths.
🚌 Long day: About 2 hours each way on the road, with Tirur and Malappuram pickups. Drop-off in reverse order: Malappuram first, then Tirur.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Conolly's Plot, museum and falls entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Shoes with good grip; Leech / insect repellent; Cash for entry fees; Light rain jacket

Headline: Ponnani & the river Nila
Description: Thunchan Parambu, the Mamankam riverbank at Tirunavaya, old Ponnani's great mosque and harbour, and the estuary where the Nila meets the sea.
Highlights: Thunchan Parambu, Mamankam riverbank, Ponnani Juma Masjid, Nila meets the sea
Itinerary:
7:45 AM — Pickup: Malappuram KSRTC bus station · Tirur railway station · Calicut Airport (on request) (Malappuram 7:45 · Tirur 8:30)
9:00 AM — Thunchan Parambu, Tirur: Birthplace of Ezhuthachan, the father of Malayalam. (Check timings)
10:30 AM — Tirunavaya: Navamukunda temple and the old Mamankam riverbank. (Temple dress code)
12:15 PM — Ponnani Juma Masjid: 16th-century mosque of Zainuddin Makhdoom. Lunch after, own expense. (Seen from outside)
2:30 PM — Ponnani harbour & beach: Fishing boats, the lighthouse and the river mouth. (No sea bathing)
4:15 PM — Padinjarekkara estuary: The sandbar where the Nila and the Tirur river meet the sea.
6:00 PM — Drop-off: Malappuram, Tirur station, Calicut Airport, or your own stop on the way
Good_To_Know:
🛕 Temple & mosque: Tirunavaya: men usually go in shirtless, women in saree or churidar; entry inside is at the temple's discretion. Ponnani Juma Masjid is a working mosque — we see it from outside; entry inside only if the committee allows.
👗 What to wear: Clothes covering shoulders and knees for the temple and the mosque area. Sandals that slip off easily.
🌊 At the sea: The river mouth has strong currents and shifting sand — paddling and swimming are not allowed on this tour. Monsoon (June–Sept): beach stops are short or skipped.
🗓️ Fridays: Friday midday prayers make Ponnani town very busy — we may reverse the order on Fridays. Pickup times are shared the evening before.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch; Any entry or offerings; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Clothes covering shoulders and knees; Slip-on sandals; Hat and sunscreen; Cash for offerings & snacks

Headline: Kadalundi birds & boats
Description: Birds on the Kadalundi mudflats, dhows built by hand at Beypore, a walk out on the breakwater, then Kozhikode's halwa street and a beach sunset.
Highlights: Kadalundi birds, Beypore dhow yard, Breakwater walk, Kozhikodan halwa
Itinerary:
7:45 AM — Pickup: Malappuram KSRTC bus station · Tirur railway station · Calicut Airport (on request) (Malappuram 7:45 · Tirur 8:30)
9:30 AM — Kadalundi bird sanctuary: Mangroves and mudflats at the river mouth — herons and migrants. (Boat ride paid direct)
11:45 AM — Beypore uru yard: Craftsmen building giant wooden dhows by hand. (Ask before photos)
12:30 PM — Beypore breakwater: Walk out to sea at the Chaliyar mouth. Lunch after, own expense. (No sea bathing)
2:45 PM — SM Street, Kozhikode: The old sweet street — Kozhikodan halwa and the bazaar. (Walking street)
4:00 PM — Kozhikode beach: Seafront promenade, old pier pillars and sunset snacks.
7:15 PM — Drop-off: Malappuram, Tirur station, Calicut Airport, or your own stop on the way
Good_To_Know:
🐦 Birding: November to April is the best season for migrant birds; a few resident birds all year. Low tide shows the most birds — timings shift with the tide, we plan around it.
⛵ Uru yard: The dhow yards are working sites — watch from where the craftsmen allow, away from timber and tools. Work stops on some days; you may see a hull, not a full build.
🌊 Sea & breakwater: Walk only on the paved top of the breakwater; no climbing on the side rocks. No sea bathing on this tour; in rough monsoon weather the breakwater may be closed.
🚌 Long day: Drop-off from about 6:30 PM: Tirur first, then Malappuram. Calicut Airport drop on request — tell us when you book.
Inclusions: Shared seat, solo to 15; Water & snacks; Free drop within the city; Caretaker for 10+ guests
Exclusions: Lunch and snacks; Boat ride at Kadalundi; Tolls and parking (private trips)
What_To_Carry: Binoculars if you have them; Hat and sunscreen; Comfortable walking shoes; Cash for the boat & halwa

Headline: Malappuram hills & Ayurveda
Description: Morning mist on Kodikuthimala, the 'Ooty of Malappuram', then Kottakkal's century-old Arya Vaidya Sala and a sunset over the town from Kottakkunnu hill.
Highlights: Kodikuthimala views, Hilltop watchtower, Kottakkal Ayurveda, Kottakkunnu sunset
Itinerary:
7:15 AM — Pickup: Malappuram KSRTC bus station · Tirur railway station · Calicut Airport (on request) (Tirur 7:15 · Malappuram 8:00)
9:00 AM — Kodikuthimala: A breezy hilltop with a watchtower and wide views over the Valluvanad hills. (Entry own expense)
2:00 PM — Kottakkal Arya Vaidya Sala: Kerala's famous Ayurveda house, founded in 1902: the old campus, temple front and medicine shop. Lunch in Kottakkal before, own expense. (Outside visit)
4:00 PM — Kottakkunnu hill park: Gardens on the old fort hill above Malappuram town — the best sunset view in town. (Entry own expense)
6:30 PM — Drop-off: Malappuram, Tirur station, Calicut Airport, or your own stop on the way
Good_To_Know:

Headline: Wayanad caves & forests

Day 1 · afternoon — Banasura Sagar Dam: India's largest earth dam, with green islands in the reservoir. (Entry & boating own expense)
Day 2 · morning — Edakkal Caves: A short, steep climb to caves with prehistoric rock carvings. (Closed Mondays · entry own expense)

Headline: Beypore urus & birds
Description: Kozhikode's sea-faring south: shipwrights building wooden urus by hand, a breakwater walk into the Arabian Sea at Beypore, and migratory birds on the Kadalundi estuary.

Itinerary:

🐦 Bird season: Migratory birds peak from November to April; the rest of the year you see resident herons, egrets and kingfishers. Low tide in the morning or late afternoon shows the most birds — we time it on the day.
🌊 Breakwater: The pulimuttu is a long stone breakwater; no climbing on the boulders and no walk in rough sea. In the monsoon and on high-wave alerts it is closed — we spend longer at the uru yard.
🚢 The uru yard: It is a working family yard, not a museum: keep clear of tools and timber. Ask before taking photos of the workers.
🛶 Boats: Kadalundi boat rides are run by local operators, paid direct; life jackets for everyone. No boats after dusk or when the river is high.

Headline: Waterfalls of Thusharagiri
Description: The 'misty peaks' of Kozhikode: a forest trail to the three Thusharagiri falls on the Chalippuzha, then the rock-ribbed cascades of Arippara near Thiruvambady.

Itinerary:

🚫 No bathing: Bathing and climbing on the rocks are not allowed at Thusharagiri or Arippara — currents are strong and water rises suddenly. Lives have been lost at these falls; please follow the guards.
🚯 Plastic-free: No disposable plastic inside the eco-tourism area; bags may be checked at the gate. Bring a reusable bottle; we carry the rubbish back.

Headline: Bekal fort & beach
Description: Kasaragod's coast in one easy day: the old Malik Dinar mosque, Chandragiri fort above the river mouth, the great keyhole walls of Bekal Fort and a sunset on Bekal beach.
Highlights: Bekal Fort, Chandragiri Fort, Malik Dinar Mosque, Bekal beach sunset
Itinerary:
8:00 AM — Pickup: Kasaragod railway station · Kasaragod KSRTC bus station · Kanhangad station (Kanhangad pickup from 7:15 AM)
8:30 AM — Malik Dinar Mosque, Thalangara: One of Kerala's oldest mosques, linked to Malik ibn Dinar; Thalangara is also known for its white prayer caps. (Modest dress · viewed respectfully)
9:30 AM — Chandragiri Fort & river: A 17th-century laterite fort on the hill where the Chandragiri river meets the sea. (Uneven ground)
11:00 AM — Bekal Fort: Kerala's largest fort: keyhole-shaped walls, an observation tower and the sea on three sides. Lunch nearby, own expense. (Entry own expense)
3:00 PM — Bekal Beach Park, Pallikere: Palm-shaded beach park beside the fort — a stroll, sea breeze and the sunset. (Swim only where flagged)
6:00 PM — Drop-off: Kasaragod, Kanhangad, or your own stop on the way
Good_To_Know:
🏰 Fort timings: Bekal Fort is protected by the ASI and listed as open daily, about 8 AM to 5:30 PM. Timings can change — we re-confirm the day before and adjust the order if needed.
🕌 Mosque visit: Shoulders, arms and knees covered; women carry a scarf for the head. We avoid Friday midday prayers and view the mosque respectfully from the grounds.
🌊 Beach safety: Sea bathing only where lifeguards allow; none at all in the monsoon (June–September). The fort walls have open edges — keep children close.
☀️ Heat: Bekal Fort has almost no shade by late morning. Carry a hat, water and sunscreen; the beach park has shade under the palms.

Exclusions: Lunch; Fort and beach park entry; Tolls and parking (private trips)

Headline: Ranipuram hills & meadows
Description: Kasaragod's 'Ooty': a forest trail through shola woods to the grassy top of Ranipuram on the Karnataka border, then Kanhangad's old Hosdurg Fort and the quiet caves of Nithyanandashram.
Highlights: Shola forest trail, Hilltop meadows, Hosdurg Fort, Ashram caves
Itinerary:
7:00 AM — Pickup: Kasaragod railway station · Kasaragod KSRTC bus station · Kanhangad station (Kanhangad pickup 7:45 AM)
9:30 AM — Ranipuram trek: About 2.5 km each way through shola forest to open meadows and views over the Kodagu hills. Allow 3 hours. (Forest ticket own expense)
1:00 PM — Lunch near Panathady: Simple Kerala meals at the base or in Rajapuram, own expense.
3:45 PM — Hosdurg Fort & Nithyanandashram: Kanhangad's round-bastioned Keladi fort, and the ashram's 45 rock-cut meditation caves next to it. (Quiet · modest dress)

Good_To_Know:

🌧️ Season: Greenest from June to January; mist and leeches in the monsoon. If the trail is closed for weather or elephants, we tell you early and offer another date.
🚯 Plastic-free: Disposable plastic is not allowed inside; bottles may be checked at the counter. Bring a reusable bottle; we carry all rubbish back.

Description: Lord Ayyappa's gold ornaments leave Pandalam for Sabarimala, two days before Makaravilakku. See them at Valiyakoikkal temple, watch the send-off, then meet the procession on its route. Event dates: ≈Tue 12 Jan 2027 · from Pandalam (Estimate — confirm with Pandalam palace / TDB).

🐘 The vela: The festival of Nellikulangara Bhagavathy, shared by the villages of Nenmara and Vallangi, on the 20th of Meenam. The flag goes up on Meenam 1; the vela day brings elephants, melam, lit pavilions and night fireworks.
🚧 Roads & crowds: Police close roads around the venue on the main days. Your driver drops you at the nearest open point and you walk the last stretch. Agree a meeting point and time with the driver before you get out — phone networks jam in big crowds.
📅 Date: We expect the vela on Saturday 3 April 2027. The temple and the two desams fix the programme — we re-confirm before your trip.
🎆 Fireworks: Stand where the police allow, well back from the firing ground; ear plugs help. Keep children close — crowds surge when the display starts and ends.
